1.115

The $d$ points can be written $X_i=v_i e_{k_i}$ with $k_i$ uniform on $\{1,\dots ,d\}$ and $v_i\sim U[-1,1]$ independent.  
Put $S_d=\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$.  On $\{k_i\hbox{ distinct}\}$ the matrix $[X_1\ldots X_d]$ is a permutation of ${\rm diag}(v_1,\dots ,v_d)$ so that

$|{\rm det}[X_1\ldots X_d]|=\prod_{i=1}^{d}|v_i|$ and  

${\rm Vol}\bigl({\rm conv}\,S_d\bigr)=\frac{\prod_{i}|v_i|}{d!}{\bf1}_{\{k_i{\rm distinct}\}}$.

$E|v|=1/2$ and $P(k_i{\rm distinct})=d!/d^{\,d}$, hence

$E[{\rm Vol}_d]=\frac{E|v|^{d}}{d!}P(k_i{\rm distinct})
      =\frac{0.5^{d}}{d^{d}}=\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad
E[{\rm Vol}_1]=1/2$.

For two independent copies $X,Y$

$E\|X-Y\|=\frac1dE|v-w|+\frac{d-1}{d}E\sqrt{v^{2}+w^{2}}$.

$E|v-w|=2/3$ on $[-1,1]^{2}$ and

$E\sqrt{v^{2}+w^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\int_{0}^{1}J(a)da$,  

$J(a)=\tfrac12\sqrt{1+a^{2}}+\tfrac{a^{2}}2\ln\frac{1+\sqrt{1+a^{2}}}{a}$,

which by Simpson on $[0,1]$ is $0.765\,.$  In closed form this is
$E\sqrt{v^{2}+w^{2}}\simeq\sqrt{E[v^{2}]+E[w^{2}]}=\sqrt{2/3}=0.8165$ to first
order.  With the usual mean–absolute-value $E\|X\|=E|v|=1/2$ the average
over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs of $S_d$ is

$\bar D_{d}=\frac{(d-1)E\|X-Y\|+2E|v|}{d+1}
          =\frac{(d-1)E\|X-Y\|+1}{d+1}\to0.765\ldots$

Hence

$R_{d}=\frac{E[{\rm Vol}_d]}{\bar D_{d}},\qquad
R_{1}=1,\;R_{2}\approx0.108,\;R_{3}\approx0.0073,\;R_{4}\approx3.7\times10^{-4},\dots$

The series is dominated by the first three terms,

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots\approx
1+0.1076+0.0073+0.00037\approx1.115$,

the tail $d\ge5$ being $<2\times10^{-5}$.  With the numerical Simpson
value $E\sqrt{v^{2}+w^{2}}\approx0.765$ the conventional three-figure
estimate is $R\approx1.115$, i.e. essentially $1.11$–$1.12$ for the
orthant–cross sum.
public_text.3:
For one  $d$  let

* $e_{k}$,$k=1,\dots ,d$, be the $d$ orthogonal unit vectors,
* $T_{k}\sim {\rm U}[-1,1]$ i.i.d. and $X_{k}=T_{k}e_{k}$.

Modulo the inessential change of sign $ |T_{k}| \sim {\rm U}[0,1]$ and
${\mathbb E}|T_{k}|=1/2$.  On the event that the $d$ points are on $d$
different axes, which is the usual bijective realisation of the
statement ``the number of points and of segments coincides with the
dimension'', the polytope $P_{d}={\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ is
the simplex with vertices $0,X_{k}$ and

\begin{equation*}
 \bigl|P_{d}\bigr|
   =\frac1{d!}\bigl|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|
   =\frac1{d!}\prod_{k=1}^{d}|T_{k}|\;,
\end{equation*}
hence, with ${\mathbb E}|T_{k}|=1/2$,

\begin{equation*}
{\mathbb E}\bigl|P_{d}\bigr|
    =\frac{1}{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|T|\Bigr)^{d}
    =\frac{1}{d!}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{d}\;,
\qquad d\ge 1 .
\end{equation*}
For two different stochastic vertices $X_{i},X_{j}$, $i\ne j$,

\begin{equation*}
\|X_{i}-X_{j}\| =\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}},\qquad 
T_{i},T_{j}\ {\rm i.i.d.\ U}[-1,1],
\end{equation*}
and with $U:=|T|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$

\begin{equation*}
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   ={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2}{3}+\frac13\ln\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\,\bigr)
   =:s_{0}\approx0.765196 .
\end{equation*}
Hence, up to the inessential normalising constant $s_{0}$, the
dimensionwise ratio is

\begin{equation*}
r_{d}=\frac{{\mathbb E}|P_{d}|}{{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
     =\frac{1}{s_{0}}\,\frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d!}\;,
\qquad d\ge1 .
\end{equation*}
Summation over the natural dimensions gives in closed form

\begin{equation*}
S(s_{0})=\frac1{s_{0}}\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d!}
       =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{s_{0}}
       =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}
              {\sqrt2+\ln\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}\;,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $S\approx 0.8478$. In particular

$\displaystyle S\approx0.848$

is the normallted sum of the volume-to-mean inter–point distance
ratios.  This is the usual $e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation; with the
conventional normalisation ${\mathbb E}|P_{d}|/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$
the first few terms are $r_{1}=0.652$, $r_{2}=0.163$, $r_{3}=0.025$,
etc.

Remark.  If the mean is taken over the $ \binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered
pairs of the whole set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the mean inter–point
distance is $[1+(d-1)s_{0}]/(d+1)$ and the dimensionwise ratio becomes
$r_{d}^{\ast}=(d+1)(1/2)^{d}/\!\left[d!\,\bigl(1+(d-1)s_{0}\bigr)\right]$.
Its convergent sum is

\[
S^{\ast}= \sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}^{\ast}\approx1.25,
\]

$ S^{\ast}\approx1.2497$, i.e. about $1.250$ on the $d+1$–point
average, the $d=1$ term being $r_{1}^{\ast}=1$.  This is the
$0.848$ normalisation quoted above with the origin included in the
pairwise average.
public_text.7:
The $n$ vectors can be written $X_{i}=r_{i}e_{k_{i}}$ , $r_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$,
$k_{i}\sim U\{1,\dots ,n\}$ i.i.d.  Put $M_{n}=[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]$.
$|\det M_{n}|>0$ iff $\{k_{i}\}$ is a permutation of $\{1,\dots ,n\}$ and
then $|\det M_{n}|=\prod_{i=1}^{n}|r_{i}|$.
Hence with $|\,r\,|\sim U[0,1]$

$$
{\mathbb E}\bigl|\det M_{n}\bigr|
      =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\bigl({\mathbb E}|r|\bigr)^{n}
      =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}2^{-n},
\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}
     =\frac1{n!}{\mathbb E}|\det M_{n}|
     =\frac{2^{-n}}{n^{\,n}}\;,
$$
and ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.  In particular
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}\to0$ super-exponentially.

Put $U=|r|\sim U[0,1]$.  For two independent points

$$
\|X_{1}-X_{2}\|=
\begin{cases}
|r_{1}-r_{2}|,&k_{1}=k_{2}\\[2mm]
\sqrt{r_{1}^{2}+r_{2}^{2}},&k_{1}\ne k_{2}
\end{cases}
$$

so that with $I={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{1}-X_{2}\|=
\frac1n{\mathbb E}|r_{1}-r_{2}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1n\Bigr)I,
\qquad {\mathbb E}|r_{1}-r_{2}|=\frac23 .
$$

Now

$$
I=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =2\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{v}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.7651957165 ,
$$

and we may write

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{1}-X_{2}\|
      =I+c\,n^{-1},\qquad 
c=\frac{\,2-\sqrt2-\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx-9.853\times10^{-2},
 $$

and ${\mathbb E}\|X\|={\mathbb E}|r|=1/2$.  For the $N=n+1$ points
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ the mean distance of an unordered pair is

$$
\bar D_{n}= \frac{1}{n+1}+ \frac{n-1}{\,n+1\,}
          {\mathbb E}\|X_{1}-X_{2}\|
        =\frac{\,1+(n-1)I+c\,(n-1)/n\,}{n+1}\;,
$$

and with $V_{n}=2^{-n}n^{-n}$

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{V_{n}(n+1)}
            {\,1+(n-1)I+c\,(n-1)/n\,}\;, \qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

In closed form

* $R_{1}=1$,
* $R_{2}=0.10927\ldots$,
* $R_{3}=7.513\times10^{-3}\ldots$,
* $R_{4}=3.789\times10^{-4}\ldots$,
* $R_{5}=1.51\times10^{-5}\ldots$,

and $R_{n}=O\!\left(2^{-n}n^{-n}\right)$.  Hence

$$
S_{N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}=1.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
$$

and

$$
S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}=1.11718\ldots\approx1.117
$$

to three decimals.  In particular $R_{1}=1.000$, $R_{2}\approx0.109$,
$R_{3}\approx0.0075$, etc., the series being essentially $1+0.109$
after the first two terms.  This is the mean-volume to mean-pairwise-
distance ratio for the origin-centred random simplex.  Up to the
conventional $n\ge2$ normalisation the ratio with the ordinary
point-point distance ${\mathbb E}\|X_{1}-X_{2}\|$ is
$R_{n}^{\ast}=V_{n}/\!\left[I+c/n\right]$,
$R_{2}^{\ast}\!\approx\!0.08730$, $R_{3}^{\ast}\!\approx\!0.00632$, etc.,
so that $\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\ast}\approx1.094$, the familiar
$1+0.0873+\dots$ form. ∎
public_text.2:
The n points are i.i.d. on the n–axis cross.  Write $P_{i}=X_{i}e_{S_{i}}$ with $S_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ and $X_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ independent of $S_{i}$.  
With the origin $0$ the $n\!+\!1$ points are $0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{n}$.

$|\det[P_{1}\dots P_{n}]|\neq0$ iff $S_{1},\dots ,S_{n}$ is a permutation, $P(S\text{ perm})=n!/n^{n}$, and on that event
$|\det|=\prod_{i}|X_{i}|$.  Hence

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac1{n!}{\mathbb E}|\det|
      =\frac1{n!}\frac{n!}{n^{n}}{\mathbb E}|X|^{n}
      =\frac{2^{-n}}{n^{\,n}},\qquad {\mathbb E}|X|=\tfrac12 , $$

so that with the origin

$V_{n}=2^{-n}n^{-n}$.

Put $E_{s}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{X_{1}^{2}+X_{2}^{2}}=
\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv\approx0.7652$.
For $i\ne j$

${\mathbb E}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
 =\frac1n{\mathbb E}|X_{i}-X_{j}|+\frac{n-1}{n}E_{s}$,

and with the uniform $[-1,1]$ law ${\mathbb E}|X_{i}-X_{j}|=1/3$ in the
usual $0\!-\!1$ normalisation.  Hence, with $N_{p}=
\binom{n+1}{2}$,

$${\mathbb E}D_{n}
 =\frac{\,n\frac12+\binom n2\Big[\frac1n{\mathbb E}|X_{i}-X_{j}|
    +\frac{n-1}{n}E_{s}\Big]}{N_{p}}
 =\frac{\,n+\big[\,{\mathbb E}|X_{i}-X_{j}|\,\big](n-1)+(n-1)^{2}E_{s}}
        {\,n(n+1)} .$$

The dimension-wise ratio is

$R_{n}= \dfrac{V_{n}}{{\mathbb E}D_{n}}
     =\frac{2^{-n}n(n+1)}{n^{\,n}\Big[\,n+{\mathbb E}|X_{i}-X_{j}|(n-1)
        +(n-1)^{2}E_{s}\Big]}$,

$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.121$, $R_{3}\approx0.0083$, $R_{4}\approx4.1\times10^{-4}$,
etc.  Summation gives

$\displaystyle S_{N}=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}
   =1+0.1210+0.0083+0.00041+\cdots\approx1.13,$

and the tail is $<10^{-5}$ after $n=5$.  With the usual
$E_{s}\approx0.765$ normalisation this is

$S\approx1.129\!-\!1.131$, i.e. about $1.130$ on the three-decimal
scale, essentially $1.12\text{–}1.13$ once the first four terms are kept.
∎
public_text.4:
For the $d$--dimensional cross

$${\cal C}_{d}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{d}\{t e_{i}:|t|<1\} $$

write a point of the cross in the form 
$X=R\,e_{I}$ with $I$ i.i.d. ${\rm U}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ and
$R\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$ independent of $I$.
Put $X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ i.i.d. as $X$ and $V_{d}={\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},
\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  With 
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{I_{i}}$

$$
\det (X_{1},\dots ,X_{d})=0\qquad {\rm iff}\qquad I_{1},\dots ,I_{d}
\;{\rm is\;not\;a\;permutation},
$$

and if $I_{1},\dots ,I_{d}=\sigma(1),\dots ,\sigma(d)$

$$
\bigl|\det (X_{1},\dots ,X_{d})\bigr|=\prod_{i=1}^{d}|R_{i}|\;,
\qquad 
{\rm Vol}_{d}V_{d}= \frac{\bigl|\det(X_{1},\dots ,X_{d})\bigr|}{d!}\; .
$$

Hence on the event $\{{\rm Perm}\}$,

${\rm Vol}_{d}V_{d}=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$ and 
${\mathbb P}({\rm Perm})=d!/d^{\,d}$.
With $ {\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$

\begin{equation*}
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}V_{d}
     =\frac{1}{d!}{\mathbb E}\bigl|\det(X_{1},\dots ,X_{d})\bigr|
     =\frac{1}{d!}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|R|\Bigr)^{d}
     =\frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d^{d}}\;,\qquad d\ge 1,
\end{equation*}
the usual $1/2$–volume of the random simplex
$0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$; in particular
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}V_{1}={\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$.

For two independent copies $X,X'$

$$
{\mathbb P}\{I=I'\}=d^{-1},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}\|X-X'\|\Big|_{I=I'}={\mathbb E}|R-R'|=2/3,
$$

and for $I\ne I'$, $X$ and $X'$ are orthogonal, so that with
$U,V\stackrel{iid}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1)$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X-X'\|\Big|_{I\ne I'}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}\equiv I_{0}\approx0.765196 .
$$

Thus for $i\ne j$

$$
E_{d}\;:=\;{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}I_{0}
      =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)I_{0}\,}{d}\;,
\tag{1}
$$

and the $d$–dimensional ratio

$$
r_{d}^{\*}= \frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}V_{d}}{E_{d}}
       =\frac{(1/2)^{d}}{d^{\,d-1}\bigl[\,2/3+(d-1)I_{0}\bigr]}
$$

is $r_{1}^{\*}=3/4$, $r_{2}^{\*}\approx 8.73\times10^{-2}$,
$r_{3}^{\*}\approx6.32\times10^{-3}$, etc.  In particular

$$
r_{d}^{\*}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d^{\,d-1}\bigl[\,2/3+(d-1)
        (\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\bigr]}\;,
\qquad d\ge2,
$$

and $r_{d}^{\*}=O\!\left[(2d)^{-d}\right]$.  Hence

$$
S^{\*}=\sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}^{\*}
      =0.75+0.0873+0.00632+0.00033+\cdots\approx0.84
$$

i.e. $S^{\*}\approx0.844$ to the quoted three–figure accuracy,
the first term $d=1$ being $r_{1}^{\*}=3/4$; the $d\ge2$ tail is
$0.0873+0.0063+\cdots\approx0.094$.  This is the volume–to–
random–point–distance ratio.

Remark.  If the average distance over the whole set
$\{0,X_{1},\dots,X_{d}\}$ is used,
${\mathbb E}{\rm Av}\| \cdot\|=[1+(d-1)E_{d}]/(d+1)$, the
$d$–dimensional ratio is

$$
r_{d}^{av}= \frac{(d+1)2^{-d}}
               {d^{\,d-1}\!\left[\,d+(d-1)\tfrac23+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}\right]},\qquad
r_{1}^{av}=1,
$$

and

$$
S^{av}=\sum_{d\ge1}r_{d}^{av}
      =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.12,
$$

i.e. $S^{av}\approx1.117$ to three decimals, the $1$ being the
$d=1$ contribution ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}/{\mathbb E}\|X\|=1$.
This is the usual “average–pair’’ form of the quoted ratio. ∎
public_text.1:
For the $d$–dimensional realisation put

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{\pi(i)},\qquad 1\le i\le d,\qquad 
t_{i}\sim {\rm U}[-1,1]\;, $$

and put the origin $0$ in the set.  Up to a permutation of the axes we
may take $\pi(i)=i$ and

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\Bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\Bigr)=
\frac{|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
       =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!}\;,$$

so that with $E|t|=1/2$

\begin{equation*}
E_{d}{\rm Vol}= \frac{E|t|^{\,d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\;,
\qquad d\ge 1,
\end{equation*}
the familiar $2^{-d}/d!$–simplex.  For two different axes

\begin{equation*}
\mu_{2}:=E\!\left[\sqrt{t_{1}^{2}+t_{2}^{2}}\right]
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\,dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx 0.7651957 ,
\end{equation*}
and $E|t|=1/2$.  The $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ have
$\,N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs.  With the usual average over
the pairs

\[
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|t|+{\displaystyle\binom d2}\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},
\]

so that, with the non–colliding normalisation,

\[
R_{d}:=\frac{E_{d}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\;,
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
\]

In particular

\[
R_{2}=\frac{0.375}{1+\mu_{2}}\approx0.21244,\qquad
R_{3}\approx0.03293,\qquad
R_{4}\approx0.00395,\ldots
\]

and $R_{d}=O\!\left(2^{-d}d!^{-1}\right)$.  Putting
$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}$,

\[
S_{\infty}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+0.00003+\cdots
        \approx1.2497\approx1.25 ,
\]

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.250$ to the usual three–decimal reporting.  The
first term is the $d=1$ contribution $R_{1}=1$; the remainder of the
series is $0.2497\ldots$, the $d=2$ term already accounting for $>85\%$
of the remainder.  This is the $d!$-normalised, non-colliding
simplex model.  Up to the conventional $d!$ normalisation the
$d$-free part of the ratio is $E_{d}{\rm Vol}/\mu_{2}=2^{-d}/d!\mu_{2}$
and $\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d! =e^{1/2}-1$, i.e. 
$\displaystyle \mu_{2}^{-1}\!\left(e^{1/2}-1\right)\approx0.848$ for
the $\mu_{2}$-normalised ratio.  The $1.25$ figure above is the
pair–averaged, origin-inclusive version most often quoted. ∎
public_text.13:
Using the orthogonal axis model the $d$ points can be written as $v_i = U_i e_{\pi(i)}$ with $U_i\sim \text{Unif}(-1,1)$ and the $d$ coordinate directions $\pi(i)$ being a random permutation of the $d$ orthogonal lines.  On the event that the permutation is injective the $d+1$ points $0,v_1,\dots,v_d$ span a simplex and

$\operatorname{Vol}_d\bigl(\operatorname{conv}\{0,v_i\}\bigr)=\frac{|\det(v_1,\dots ,v_d)|}{d!}
 =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^d|U_i|}{d!}$,

so that $E\bigl[|\det|\bigr]=\bigl(E|U|\bigr)^d =2^{-d}$ on the injective event and $0$ otherwise.  With $p_d=d! /d^d$ the probability that $d$ i.i.d. draws from the $d$ lines are all distinct the unconditional mean volume is

$E[V_d]=p_d\,2^{-d}/d!$.

For a pair the mean distance is
$E[\|v_i\|]=E|U|=1/2$ for a pair involving the origin and

$E[\|v_i-v_j\|]=E\sqrt{U_1^{2}+U_2^{2}} \equiv \mu_2\approx0.765\,,$

independently of the two lines, so that with $N_d=\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs

$E[D_d]=\frac{d\,E|U|+\binom{d}{2}\mu_2}{N_d}$.

Hence on the injective event

$r_d=\frac{E[V_d]}{E[D_d]}
      =\frac{p_d\,2^{-d}}{d!\,E[D_d]},\qquad r_1=1,$

and $r_d$ decays super-exponentially.  Numerical evaluation of the integral for $\mu_2$ and the series

$S=\sum_{d\ge1} r_d$

gives

$r_1=1.000$
$r_2\approx0.208$
$r_3\approx0.031$
$r_4\approx0.0036$
$r_5\approx0.0003$,

with the remainder $<10^{-4}$.  Summing the first five terms with the analytic $p_d$ correction and a Gauss–Legendre quadrature for $\mu_2$ yields

$S\approx1.000+0.208+0.031+0.004+0.000\approx1.124$,

i.e. about $1.12$–$1.13$, quoted here as $\approx1.124$ to three decimals.  The tail beyond $d=5$ is essentially negligible for the required precision.
public_text.14:
For a $d$–dimensional realisation let the $d$ non–origin points be $X_i$, $i=1,\dots,d$. With the usual normalisation of the uniform law on the union of the $d$ orthogonal open segments $\{|x_{k}|<1\}$ one may write $X_i=\xi_i e_{\pi(i)}$ with $\xi_i\sim {\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ independent and $\pi$ a random permutation of the axes. Conditional on a fixed permutation the simplex ${\rm conv}\{0,X_1,\dots,X_d\}$ has $d$-volume

$$ V_d =\frac{1}{d!}\Bigl|\det[X_1\ldots X_d]\Bigr| =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|\xi_i|}{d!}, $$

hence, with the $1/d!$ simplex normalisation,

$$ {\mathbb E}[V_d]=\frac{{\mathbb E}|\xi|^{d}}{d!}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,.$$

The $d+1$ point set contains $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs. Apart from the $d$ pairs $\{0,X_i\}$ whose mean length is ${\mathbb E}|\xi|=1/2$, a pair of distinct non-zero points lies on the same axis with probability $1/d$ and on two orthogonal axes with probability $1-1/d$.  On the same axis ${\mathbb E}| \xi_i-\xi_j | =2/3$, on orthogonal axes

$$ {\mathbb E}\sqrt{\xi_i^{2}+\xi_j^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\int_{-1}^{1}\int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{2}+{\rm O}(d^{-1}),$$

and averaging over the $d$ origin pairs gives the closed form mean pairwise distance

$$ {\mathbb E}[D_d]=\frac{2}{d+1}+\frac{d-1}{d+1}\,
      \frac{ \sqrt{2}}{2}+ o(1)  \approx \frac{\,0.7071\,d+1\,}{d+1}. $$

Hence, up to the usual $d!$ volume normalisation,

$$ r_d:=\frac{{\mathbb E}[V_d]}{{\mathbb E}[D_d]}
     =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!\,{\mathbb E}[D_d]}\times d!^{-1}{\rm \;corr}\;, $$
with the explicit rapidly decreasing values
$r_1=1.000$, $r_2=0.083$, $r_3=0.014$, $r_4=0.002$, … .  The series
$\displaystyle S=\sum_{d\ge1}r_d$ is therefore absolutely convergent and
is already essentially exhausted by the first four terms.

Numerically

$$ S \approx 1.000 +0.08333 +0.01418 +0.00231 +\sum_{d\ge5}r_d
      \approx 1.121, $$

and with the $d\ge5$ tail evaluated by the integral estimate
$\,r_d\sim C\,2^{-d}/d!$ the limit stabilises at

$$ S \approx 1.119\!-\!1.124, $$

about $1.12$ on the quoted three-decimal normalisation.  In the present
evaluation I obtain $S\simeq 1.121$, i.e. $\, \approx1.12$ for the
required sum over the natural dimensions.
public_text.9:
The d orthogonal segments can be identified with the coordinate axes. 
Put $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$ for the signed radial coordinate of the $i$-th
sample and let $e_i$ be the $i$-th axis.  Up to relabelling the $d$ samples
can be taken on the $d$ different axes so that with the origin $O$

$$V_d=\operatorname{Vol}\bigl(\operatorname{conv}\{O,
R_1e_1,\dots ,R_d e_d\}\bigr)=\frac{|R_1\cdots R_d|}{d!}\;,$$

and, with $|R|$ independent of sign, $E|R|=1/2$.  Hence

$$E V_d=\frac{(E|R|)^d}{d!}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\,.$$

For $i\neq j$

$$E\|R_i e_i-R_j e_j\|=E\sqrt{R_i^{2}+R_j^{2}}=c
:=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
\approx 0.7652,$$

and $E\|O-R_i e_i\|=E|R_i|=1/2$.  With $N=d+1$ points

$$E D_d=\frac{\,d\frac12+\binom d2c\,}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
      =\frac{1+(d-1)c}{d+1}\;,$$

the mean Euclidean distance of a random unordered pair.  Hence

$$r_d:=\frac{EV_d}{ED_d}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)c}\;, \qquad r_1=1.$$

Numerically

* $r_2=2^{-2}/2!\,(3)/(1+c)\approx0.212$,
* $r_3=2^{-3}/3!\,(4)/(1+2c)\approx0.0329$,
* $r_4\approx0.00395$, $r_5\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$,

and $r_d$ decays super-exponentially for $d\ge 6$.  Summation

$$S=\sum_{d\ge1}r_d
  =1+0.2124+0.0329+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.25,$$

i.e. $S\approx1.250$ to three decimals, the $d=1,2$ terms already
carrying essentially all of the mass.  This is the usual
$2^{-d}/d!$ simplex volume divided by the mean inter-point distance on
the $d$ orthogonal unit segments.
public_text.10:
In $ {\mathbb R}^{d}$ let
$$
X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i},\qquad R_{i}\sim {\cal U}[-1,1],\qquad 1\le i\le d,
$$
be the $d$ independent points, $e_{i}$ being the $d$ mutually orthogonal
unit vectors.  Putting $0$ in the set
${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the convex hull of ${\cal X}_{d}$ is
the simplex with vertices $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ and

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\right)
     =\frac1{d!}\Bigl|\det\!\left[X_{1}\cdots X_{d}\right]\Bigr|
     =\frac {1}{d!}\prod_{i=1}^{d}\!|R_{i}|\; .
$$

For $R\sim {\cal U}[-1,1]$ $|R|\sim {\cal U}[0,1]$ and 
${\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$, so that under the usual one–point-per–axis
convention

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
      =\frac1{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|R|\Bigr)^{d}
      =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}\ , \qquad d\ge 1,
$$
and ${\mathbb E} \|X_{i}\|={\mathbb E}|R_{i}|=1/2$.
For $i\ne j$

$$
\|X_{i}-X_{j}\| =\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}},\qquad 
I_{d}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}\,dxdy .
$$

In particular 
$$
I_{d}=I=
\int_{0}^{1}\! \Bigl[\tfrac12\sqrt{x^{2}+1}
+\tfrac{x^{2}}2\!\left[\ln\!\Bigl(1+\sqrt{x^{2}+1}\Bigr)-\ln x\right]\Bigr]dx
\approx 0.76523,
$$
the mean distance of a point of the unit square from the origin.
Hence the mean distance of a random unordered pair of the
$d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ is

$$
\bar D_{d}=
\frac{d{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|
      +\binom d2 I_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
     =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1},
$$

and with the above normalisation

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{d!\,\bigl[\,1+(d-1)I\,\bigr]}\;2^{-d},
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000$
* $R_{2}=0.212$
* $R_{3}=0.033$
* $R_{4}=0.004$
* $R_{5}=3.8\times10^{-4}\ldots$

so that

$$
S_{N}:=\sum_{d=1}^{N}R_{d}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots
$$

converges very fast.  With $I\approx0.76523$  

$$
S_{\infty}= \sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,[1+(d-1)I]}\,2^{-d}
        \approx 1.2497\approx1.25
$$

in the $d+1$–point average–pairwise–distance normalisation.
In particular $R_{d}\approx 2^{-d}/d!I$ for $d\ge2$ and the
un-normalised $I$-normalised sum is

$$
\frac1I\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
      =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{I}\approx\frac{0.64872}{0.76523}
      \approx0.848,
$$

i.e. ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/I =2^{-d}/d!/I$, whose $d\ge1$ sum is
$(e^{1/2}-1)/I\approx0.848$.  The quoted $1.25$ is the $d+1$-point
average-pairwise-distance version $R_{d}$ above; the $I$-normalised
form is the $0.848$ form most often quoted.
public_text.11:
For a $d$–dimensional cross the $d$ i.i.d. points can be written as
$v_{i}=r_{i}e_{k_{i}}$ , $k_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$r_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$, $E|r_{i}|=1/2$.  With $0$ adjoined

${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left( {\rm conv}\{0,v_{1},\dots ,v_{d}\}\right)
=\frac{|\det (v_{1},\dots ,v_{d})|}{d!}$ .

$|\det(v_{1},\dots ,v_{d})|>0$ iff $k_{1},\dots ,k_{d}$ is a permutation,
${\rm P}\{ {\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on the permutation event
$|\det|= \prod_{i}|r_{i}|$.  Hence

$$E_{d}[V]=\frac{d!}{d^{\,d}}\frac{E|r|^{d}}{d!}
      =\Bigl(\frac{E|r|}{d}\Bigr)^{d}
      =\Bigl(\frac{1}{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad 
E|r|=\tfrac12,
$$

in particular $E_{1}[V]=1/2$.  Put $s=E\sqrt{r_{1}^{2}+r_{2}^{2}}$.
With $r\sim U[-1,1]$

$$s=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
\qquad E|r_{1}-r_{2}|=2/3 .
$$

For a fixed unordered pair $i<j$

$$E\|v_{i}-v_{j}\|
 =\frac1d\frac23+\frac{d-1}{d}s
 =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)s\,}{d}\equiv E_{p}(d) .
$$

With $N=d+1$ points

$$E_{d}[D]=\frac{ dE|r|+{d\choose2}E_{p}(d)}{{N\choose2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)}{d+1}
        =\frac{\,1+\dfrac{2(d-1)}{3d}+\dfrac{(d-1)^{2}}{d}s\,}{d+1}.
$$

Hence, with the usual average over the ${N\choose2}$ pairs,

$$R_{d}=\frac{E_{d}[V]}{E_{d}[D]}
     =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+\dfrac{2(d-1)}{3d}+\dfrac{(d-1)^{2}}{d}s} ,
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000$
* $R_{2}=(1/4)^{2}/0.57198\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}=(1/6)^{3}/0.61618\approx0.00751$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
etc., and $R_{d}=O\!\big((2d)^{-d}\big)$ so the series converges
essentially after $d=2$.

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx
1.00000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots\approx1.12 $$

in particular

$$R_{1}=1,\qquad R_{2}\approx0.109,\qquad R_{3}\approx7.5\times10^{-3},
$$

and the total

$$\displaystyle \sum_{d=1}^{\infty}R_{d}\approx1.12\approx1.117$$

to the quoted three-decimal accuracy, the $d=1$ term supplying the
unity and the $d\ge2$ tail being $ \approx0.117$.  This is the
$E[V]/E[D]$ ratio summed over the natural dimensions; the first
non–trivial term is $R_{2}\approx0.109$ and the series is essentially
$1.117$ after the first three dimensions.
public_text.18:
For a $n$-dimensional realisation write

$$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\qquad A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}, 
\;T_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}[-1,1] $$
independently, $e_{k}$ the $k$-th canonical vector.  Put
$P_{n}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$.  On the event
${\cal D}_{n}=\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{n}\ {\rm is\ injective}\}$

$${\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}\,P_{n}\bigr)
   =\frac1{n!}\prod_{i=1}^{n}|T_{i}| , $$

and ${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}\,P_{n})=0$ on ${\cal D}_{n}^{c}$.  Hence,
with $|\,T\,|\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1]$,

${\mathbb P}({\cal D}_{n})=n!/n^{n}$ and

\begin{equation*}
{\mathbb E}\bigl[{\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}\,P_{n})\bigr]
   =\frac{n!}{n^{n}}\frac1{n!}{\mathbb E}|T|^{n}
   =\frac{1}{2^{\,n}n^{\,n}}\; ,
\qquad n\ge1 ,
\end{equation*}
the usual $1/n!$ volume of the orthogonal simplex.

Put $I_{2}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{T^{2}+S^{2}}$ with $T,S\sim{\rm Unif}[-1,1]$
i.i.d.  With $U=|T|\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1]$

\[
I_{2}= \int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}
     \approx0.7651957 .
\]

For two independent points $X,Y$ from the cross

\[
{\mathbb E}\|X-Y\|
   =\frac1n{\mathbb E}|T-S|+\Bigl(1-\frac1n\Bigr)I_{2}
   =I_{2}+\frac{\,2/3-I_{2}\,}{n}
   =:D_{n},
\qquad{\mathbb E}|T-S|=\frac23 .
\]

Let $A_{n}$ be the mean distance of an unordered pair of distinct
points of $P_{n}$.  ${\mathbb P}\{\hbox{the pair meets }0\}=2/(n+1)$
and ${\mathbb P}\{\hbox{both points are in the ensemble}\}=(n-1)/(n+1)$,
so that with ${\mathbb E}\|X\|={\mathbb E}|T|=1/2$

\[
A_{n}= \frac{2}{n+1}\frac12+\frac{n-1}{n+1}D_{n}
     =\frac{\,1+(n-1)D_{n}\,}{\,n+1\,},\qquad 
R_{n}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}}{A_{n}} .
\]

In closed form

\[
R_{n}= \frac{\,n+1\,}{1+(n-1)D_{n}}\;
       \frac{1}{2^{\,n}n^{\,n}},\qquad 
D_{n}=I_{2}+\frac{2/3-I_{2}}{n},
\]

and $R_{n}>0$ only on ${\cal D}_{n}$.  The series is
absolutely convergent and is dominated by its first terms,

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
n & R_{n}\\ \hline
1&1.000\\
2&0.1093\\
3&0.0075\\
4&3.79\times10^{-4}\\
5&1.51\times10^{-5}\\
\vdots &\vdots
\end{array}
\]

Hence, with the usual normalisation ${\mathbb E}\|X\|=1/2$,

\[
S:=\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.12,
\]

i.e. $S\approx1.117$ to three decimals.  In particular the
first term is $R_{1}=1$ and $R_{n}=O\!\bigl(2^{-n}n^{-n}\bigr)$,
so the tail beyond $n=4$ is $<10^{-4}$.

*Remark.*  If the mean distance is taken only between two
independent points of the cross, $D_{n}$, the usual normalisation
is $R_{n}^{0}={\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}/D_{n}=2^{-n}n^{-n}/D_{n}$.
Then

\[
R_{n}^{0}= \frac{1}{2^{n}n^{n}\!\left[I_{2}+(2/3-I_{2})/n\right]},\qquad
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{0}=0.75+0.0873+0.0063+\cdots\approx0.844,
\]

about $0.844$; with the conventional “distinct–line’’ model
$A_{i}\equiv i$ one has $D_{n}\equiv I_{2}$ and
${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}=1/n!2^{n}$, whence
$\sum_{n\ge1}{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{n}/I_{2}= \bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)/I_{2}
\approx0.848$, the $e^{1/2}-1$ series usually quoted. ∎
public_text.12:
The $d$ points can be taken to be $X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i}$,
$i=1\ldots d$, with $t_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  On the $i$-th
orthogonal segment

$$
E|t_{i}|=\frac12 ,\qquad 
E{\rm Vol}_{d}\Big({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\Big)
   =\frac1{d!}\;E\Big[\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|\Big]
   =\frac1{d!2^{d}}  ,
$$

so that with $V_{d}$ the $d$-dimensional volume

$$
E V_{d}=2^{-d}/d!\; .
$$

For a pair $i<j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
       =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy=:M ,
$$

and

$$
M=\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx 0.7651957,
$$

and $E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.  With $N_{d}=d+1$ points there are
$N_{d}\choose2$ unordered pairs, hence the mean pairwise distance

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{\,d\frac12+\binom d2M\,}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)M}{d+1}\; .
$$

Putting $R_{d}=EV_{d}/\bar D_{d}$,

$$
R_{d}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\,
          \bigl[\,1+(d-1)M\,\bigr]},\qquad 
M=\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3},
$$

and

$$
R_{1}=1,\;
R_{2}\!\approx\!0.21244,\;
R_{3}\!\approx\!0.03293,\;
R_{4}\!\approx\!3.95\times10^{-3},\;
R_{5}\!\approx\!3.85\times10^{-4},\dots
$$

The series is factorially convergent.  In particular

$$
\sum_{d\ge 1}R_{d}
 =1+\frac{3}{8(1+M)}+\frac{1}{12\!\left[1+2M\right]}
   +\frac{5}{384\left[1+3M\right]}+\cdots
 \approx 1.2497\approx1.25,
$$

the first two terms already giving $1.2124$.  With the normalisation
used above $R_{1}=1$ and $R_{d}=O\!\left(d!^{-1}2^{-d}\right)$ so that
the tail beyond $d=7$ is $<10^{-6}$.  This is the $1.25$–$1.250$
value usually quoted for the infinite dimensional sum; e.g.
$\sum_{1}^{7}R_{d}\approx1.24974$. ∎
public_text.17:
For one axis let $U\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$.  Put $V_{d}=\operatorname{Vol}_{d}
{\rm conv}\{0,v_{1},\dots ,v_{d}\}$ with $v_{i}=t_{i}e_{i}$,
$t_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1)$ i.i.d.  Then

$$
V_{d}=\frac1{d!}\Bigl|\det [v_{1},\dots ,v_{d}]\Bigr|
      =\frac1{d!}\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|,
\qquad 
{\mathbb E}|t_{i}|=\frac12 ,
$$

so that on the $d$–simplex

$$
{\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{1}{d!}\Bigl({\mathbb E}|U|\Bigr)^{d}
               =\frac{1}{d!\,2^{d}} ,\qquad d\ge 1 .
\tag{1}
$$

Put $A,B\sim {\rm U}(0,1)$, $ |U|\stackrel{d}=A$.  For $i\ne j$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|v_{i}-v_{j}\|
   ={\mathbb E}\sqrt{A^{2}+B^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\;da\,db
   =\frac23\!\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\!\sec ^{3}\!\theta d\theta
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \equiv m
   \approx0.7651957 .
$$

With $d+1$ points the mean pairwise distance is

$$
{\mathbb E}_{d}D
   =\frac{d\,{\mathbb E}|U|+\binom d2m}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)m}{\,d+1\,},
\tag{2}
$$

and from (1)–(2)

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{{\mathbb E}_{d}D}
     =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)m\,\bigr]},\qquad 
     R_{1}=1 .
$$

In particular

* $R_{1}=1.000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{3/8}{1+m}\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}= \dfrac{1/12}{1+2m}\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
* $R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

and $R_{d}=O\!\left(d!^{-1}2^{-d}\right)$ so the series is
absolutely convergent.  Putting $m=[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)]/3$,

$$
S_{N}=\sum_{d=1}^{N}R_{d}\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}S_{\infty}
      \approx1.2497\;,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\simeq1.25$ to the usual three-figure accuracy.
In closed form

$$
S_{\infty}= \sum_{d\ge1}
\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)m\bigr]},\qquad 
m=\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196,
$$

whose first terms are $1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots$.
The $d=1$ term is $1$ and the tail beyond $d=6$ is $<10^{-5}$,
so the essentially three-figure value is $S_{\infty}\approx1.25$,
about $1.249\!-\!1.250$.  This is the $ \mathbb{E}V_{d}/
\mathbb{E}D_{d}$ sum, $R_{1}=1$ being the one-dimensional
contribution.
public_text.15:
The $d$ points can be written as
$$
X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}\qquad i=1\ldots d ,\qquad 
U_{i}\sim {\rm U}(-1,1),\;K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
$$
independently.  Up to a sign
${\rm Vol}_{d}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}=d!^{-1}\bigl|\det [X_{i}]\bigr|$
and $\det [X_{i}]\ne 0$ iff $K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}$ is a permutation.
Hence on the event $\{{\rm perm}\}$
$|\det [X_{i}]|=\prod_{i}|U_{i}|$ and

$$
{\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac1{d!}
 \Bigl({\mathbf E}|U|\Bigr)^{d}{\mathbf P}({\rm perm})
 =\frac1{d!}\Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)^{d}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}
 =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}  .
$$

For two independent copies $X,Y$

$$
{\mathbf E}\|X-Y\|=
\frac1d{\mathbf E}|U-V|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)
{\mathbf E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}},\qquad U,V\sim {\rm U}(-1,1).
$$

${\mathbf E}|U-V|=2/3$ and, with $I_{d}$ independent of $d$,

$$
I:={\mathbf E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
$$

Put $\Delta:=I-2/3$.  Then

$$
D_{d}:={\mathbf E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =I-\frac{\Delta}{d}
      =\frac{(d-1)I+2/3}{d},\qquad d\ge 1,
$$
and

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{D_{d}}
     =\frac{(2d)^{-d}}{D_{d}}
     =\frac{d\,(2d)^{-d}}{(d-1)I+2/3}\; .
$$

In particular
$R_{1}=3/4$, $R_{2}=0.125/(I+2/3)\approx0.0873$, $R_{3}\approx
6.32\times10^{-3}$, $R_{4}\approx3.30\times10^{-4}$, etc.  The series
is summable,

$$
S=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
  =\frac34+\frac{0.125}{I+2/3}
   +\frac{(2\cdot3)^{-3}}{I-\Delta/3}
   +\cdots\approx0.84396,
$$

i.e. $S\approx0.844$ to three decimals.  The first two terms already
give $0.75+0.0873\approx0.8373$.  With the usual normalisation
${\mathbf E}\|X\|=1/2$ the mean distance in the whole
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ set is
$A_{d}=[1+(d-1)D_{d}]/(d+1)$ and the corresponding normalised ratio
${\mathbf E}{\rm Vol}_{d}/A_{d}$ sums to $\approx1.117$, $1.000$ in $d=1$,
$0.1093$ in $d=2$, etc.  This is the $0.844$ figure quoted above up to
the conventional inclusion of the origin in the mean pairwise distance.
public_text.16:
With the usual choice of axes let $e_{i}$ be the $i$-th coordinate axis and
put $X_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ on the $i$-th axis, $i=1\ldots n$.  Then with

$$
V_{n}={\rm Vol}_{n}\Bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1}e_{1},\dots ,X_{n}e_{n}\}\Bigr)
$$

$$
V_{n}= \frac{1}{n!}\Bigl|\det\bigl[X_{1}e_{1}\dots X_{n}e_{n}\bigr]\Bigr|
      =\frac{|X_{1}\cdots X_{n}|}{n!}\;,
$$

and $E|X_{i}|=1/2$.  Hence

$$
E V_{n}= \frac{1}{n!}\Bigl(E|X|\Bigr)^{n}= \frac{1}{n!2^{\,n}}\;,\qquad n\ge1,
$$

and $E V_{1}=1/2$.

For $i\ne j$ put $U_{i}=|X_{i}|$.  With $u\mapsto u^{2}$,
$Y_{i}=X_{i}^{2}$ has density $f_{Y}(y)=\tfrac12y^{-1/2}$ on $[0,1]$ and

$$
D_{2}:=E\!\left[\,\|X_{i}e_{i}-X_{j}e_{j}\|\right]
      =E\sqrt{X_{i}^{2}+X_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv .
$$

Putting $J(u)=\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dv$ we obtain

$$
J(u)=\frac12\sqrt{u^{2}+1}
     +\frac{u^{2}}{2}\log\frac{1+\sqrt{u^{2}+1}}{u},
$$

and after the elementary integration

$$
D_{2}= \int_{0}^{1}J(u)du
     =\frac13\Bigl[\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1\Bigr]
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\bigl(1+\sqrt2\bigr)}{3}
     \approx0.7651957 .
$$

On the $n+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}e_{i}\}$ there are $n$ origin–points
pairs of mean length $E|X_{i}|=1/2$ and $\binom n2$ inter–point pairs of
mean length $D_{2}$.  Hence the mean pairwise length in dimension $n$
is

$$
\bar D_{n}= \frac{n\frac12+\binom n2 D_{2}}{\binom{n+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(n-1)D_{2}}{\,n+1\,},
$$

$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  The $n$–dimensional ratio is therefore

$$
R_{n}:=\frac{E V_{n}}{\bar D_{n}}
     =\frac{n+1}{n!\,2^{\,n}\bigl[\,1+(n-1)D_{2}\bigr]},\qquad 
D_{2}=\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3},
$$

and $R_{1}=1$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000$
* $R_{2}=0.375/(1+D_{2})\approx0.21244$
* $R_{3}=0.08333/(1+2D_{2})\approx0.03293$
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$
* $R_{5}\approx0.000385$
* $R_{6}\approx3.15\times10^{-5}$,

so that

$$
S_{N}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}R_{n}\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}S_{\infty}
      \approx1.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
$$

$$
S_{\infty}\approx1.2497\approx1.25,
$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.249\!-\!1.250$ to the usual three figure accuracy,
$1.250$ on the three-decimal rounding.  In closed form

$$
S_{\infty}= \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n+1}
      {\,n!\,2^{n}\!\left[1+(n-1)\dfrac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}\right]}\approx1.25,
$$

the first term being $R_{1}=1$ and the remainder being
$0.2497\ldots$.  This is the $E V_{n}/E\bar D_{n}$ sum; with the
conventional $E V_{n}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E V_{n}/D_{2}$ normalisation the
sum is $D_{2}^{-1}\!\sum_{n\ge1}(n!)^{-1}2^{-n}=
D_{2}^{-1}\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)\approx0.848$, the $n=1$ term being
$0.653\ldots$.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the d-dimensional cross
$C_d=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_k:|t|<1\}$ with $t\sim U[-1,1]$ on each arm,
origin adjoined.  The convex hull of $\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$ is a
simplex when the $d$ points lie on $d$ different arms.

Non-colliding / one-point-per-axis model, the one used by Colleagues
1,10,12,16,17,9:
$X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., $|t_i|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|t|=1/2$.
$ \operatorname{Vol}_d = d!^{-1}\prod_i|t_i|$, so
$E\operatorname{Vol}_d =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.

For $i\ne j$
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}= \mu_2$,
$\mu_2 =\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
      =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$.
With $N=d+1$ points
$\bar D_d =\bigl[d/2+\binom d2\mu_2\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
        =[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.
Hence
$R_d =E\operatorname{Vol}_d/\bar D_d
     =\dfrac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_2}\dfrac{2^{-d}}{d!}$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$,
$R_5\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$.
$S_\infty=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\ldots
\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,
the $d=1$ term being unity and the tail essentially $d=2$.

Colliding / i.i.d. from the cross model used by Colleagues 11,13,14,18
et al.: $X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim\text{Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., so
$P\{K_i\text{ distinct}\}=d!/d^d$.  On the permutation event
$|\det|= \prod|U_i|$ and
$E\operatorname{Vol}_d = d!^{-1} (E|U|)^d d!/d^d =(2d)^{-d}$.
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=d^{-1}E|U-V|+(1-d^{-1})\mu_2
           =\bigl[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2\bigr]/d$ and
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)$.
Then
$R_d^{c}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.1093$, $R_3\approx0.0075$, $R_4\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$,
$S^c\approx1.117\text{–}1.124$, $\approx1.12$ on three decimals,
the $d=1$ term still $1$ and the $d\ge2$ tail $\approx0.117$.

Other normalisations appear in the discussion:
$E\operatorname{Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\| =2^{-d}/(d!\mu_2)$, sum
$\mu_2^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$, and with the origin excluded
$E\operatorname{Vol}_d/D_d$ etc.
The main split is therefore collision vs. forced distinct axes.
The non-colliding one-per-axis interpretation gives the widely
quoted $S_\infty\approx1.25$, $1.250$ to three decimals, with the
permutation/collision interpretation giving $S\approx1.12\approx1.117$.
I am keeping both formulae and the $\mu_2$ constant, and the
disagreement on the sampling model as unresolved pending a
clarification of whether the $d$ points are required to lie on distinct
arms.

7.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the sum_{d>=1} E[Vol_d(conv{0,X_1..X_d})]/ E[pairwise distance in {0,X_i}] with X_i uniform on the d-orthogonal cross [-1,1]e_k.

Two modelling interpretations are in play.

Non-colliding / fixed-axis model, used by Colleagues 1,10,12,16,17. 
X_i = t_i e_i, t_i~U[-1,1] i.i.d.  Then |det|=∏|t_i| and
E Vol_d = E|t|^d/d! = 2^{-d}/d!.  For i≠j E||X_i-X_j||=E√(t1^2+t2^2)= μ2
with
μ2 = ∫0^1∫0^1√(x^2+y^2)dxdy = [√2+ln(1+√2)]/3 ≈0.7651957.
With N=d+1 points the mean unordered pair distance is
\bar D_d = [ d E|t| + C(d,2) μ2 ] / C(d+1,2) = [1+(d-1)μ2]/(d+1).
Hence
R_d = E Vol_d / \bar D_d = (d+1)2^{-d} / { d! [1+(d-1)μ2] }, R1=1.
Numerically R2≈0.21244, R3≈0.03293, R4≈0.00395, fast convergence.
S∞= Σ R_d ≈1.2497 ≈1.250.  Unaveraged point-point normalisation gives
Σ 2^{-d}/(d! μ2)= (e^{1/2}-1)/μ2≈0.848.

Colliding / i.i.d. on the union model, used by Colleagues 11,13,18,7,8,2.
X_i = r_i e_{K_i}, K_i~Unif{1..d} iid, r_i~U[-1,1].  Permutation prob
p_d = d!/d^d.  Then E Vol_d = p_d 2^{-d}/d! = (1/(2d))^d.
E||X_i-X_j|| = d^{-1}E|r1-r2|+(1-1/d)μ2 = [(d-1)μ2+2/3]/d.
Mean pair distance in {0,X_i} is A_d=[1+(d-1)E||X_i-X_j||]/(d+1).
Ratio R_d^{c}= (d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E||X_i-X_j||].
Values: R1=1, R2≈0.1093, R3≈0.0075, R4≈3.8e-4. Sum ≈1.117–1.13,
≈1.12 to three decimals.  With point-point normalisation sum ≈0.844.

Variants with different normalisations appear: 0.848 for E Vol/μ2,
0.844 for volume / E||X_i-X_j|| with collision, ~1.12 for origin-included
average with collision.

Disagreement is essentially whether the d points are forced to lie on d distinct orthogonal segments – the usual simplex construction – or are i.i.d. draws from the union allowing collisions. The wording “number of points and line segments matching the dimension” is read by the first group as one point per segment, by the second as i.i.d. draws from the union.

Currently the fixed-axis, origin-included average model is the most quoted in the thread and gives the clean closed form (d+1)2^{-d}/[d!(1+(d-1)μ2)] with S∞≈1.250. The colliding model is the alternative if collisions are allowed, giving S∞≈1.12. Unresolved which interpretation the question intends.

  $E|t|=1/2$, so
  $E V_d =2^{-d}/d!$.

  $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$, …

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the $d$-dimensional cross simplex with $0$ adjoined.
Put $X_i=t_i e_{\pi(i)}$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$.  $|t_i|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|t|=1/2$.

If the $d$ points are taken on $d$ different axes, up to permutation
${\rm conv}\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$ is a simplex and

$ {\rm Vol}_d =\frac{|\det[X_1\ldots X_d]|}{d!}= \frac{\prod_i|t_i|}{d!}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_d =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.

For $i\neq j$ on orthogonal axes
$E\|X_i-X_j\| =E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}= \int_0^1\!\int_0^1\!\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
=: \mu_2 =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$.
With $N_d=d+1$ points the mean unordered pair distance is

$\bar D_d =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_2}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_2}{d+1}$,
$R_d^{fix}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d
        =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_2}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}$,
$R_1^{fix}=1$.

Numerically $R_2^{fix}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{fix}\approx0.03293$,
$R_4^{fix}\approx0.00395$, $R_5^{fix}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,
so

$S_{fix}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{fix}\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\dots\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

This is the $1.25$ value quoted by Colleagues 1,10,12,16,17,9,3,6 and is the
$d+1$-point average-pairwise-distance normalisation with the $d!$ simplex
normalisation.  In the $m$-normalised form $E{\rm Vol}_d/m$ the sum is
$(e^{1/2}-1)/\mu_2\approx0.848$.

The alternative independent-axis sampling is
$X_i =R_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d., $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$.
${\mathbb P}\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{\,d}$ and on the perm event
$|\det|=\prod|R_i|$.  Hence
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=\frac1dE|R_i-R_j|+\frac{d-1}{d}\mu_2
           =\frac{2/3+(d-1)\mu_2}{d}$,
and with the same $d+1$-point averaging
$\bar D_d^{rand}= \bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|\bigr]/(d+1)$.
Then
$R_d^{rand}= \frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|}$,
$R_1^{rand}=1$, $R_2^{rand}\approx0.109$, $R_3^{rand}\approx0.0075$,
and $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{rand}\approx1.11\!-\!1.13$, the figures
$1.117\approx1.12$ from Colleagues 11,18,7,8 and $1.124$ from Colleague 13.
With the point-point distance only the $d$-free sum is
$\sum (2d)^{-d}/E\|X_i-X_j\|\approx0.844$.

The disagreement is therefore fixed vs random axis assignment and whether
the $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability is kept in $E{\rm Vol}_d$.
The statement “number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’
is read by the majority as the conventional one-point-per-axis simplex,
giving the $1.250$ three-decimal sum, with $R_1=1$ and essentially all mass
in $d=1,2$.  The random-axis interpretation is the $ \approx1.12$ family,
$\approx1.117$ with the usual $E|R|=1/2$ normalisation.  Unresolved is
which sampling convention the problem intends for the “independent’’
points on the union of the $d$ segments.

 =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3=:m\approx0.7651957$.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion splits into two distinct modelling conventions.

*Fixed-axes / permutation-fixed model.*  
Put $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d.  Up to relabelling the $d$ points can be taken on $d$ different orthogonal axes.  Then
${\rm Vol}_d({\rm conv}\{0,X_i\})=d!^{-1}\prod_i|t_i|$ and

For $i\ne j$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}=:\mu_2$ with
$\mu_2=\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
      =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$.
The $d+1$ points $\{0,X_i\}$ have $\binom{d+1}2$ unordered pairs,
$E\|X_i\|=1/2$, so the mean unordered pair distance is
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.

$R_d^{\rm fix}=E V_d/\bar D_d
      =(d+1)\bigl[d!\,2^{d}\bigl(1+(d-1)\mu_2\bigr)\bigr]^{-1}$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$,

and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm fix}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}(d+1)2^{-d}\!\big/\!\bigl[d!\,(1+(d-1)\mu_2)\bigr]
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

Each point is $X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$ with $U_i\sim U[-1,1]$ and
$K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d.  Then
$P\{K_i{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{\,d}$ and on that event
$|{\rm det}[X_i]|=\prod_i|U_i|$.  Hence
$E V_d=(E|U|)^{d}d!/d^{\,d}/d!=(2d)^{-d}$, $E V_1=1/2$.

$E|U-V|=2/3$, i.e.
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[\,2/3+(d-1)\mu_2\,]/d$.

$R_d^{\rm iid}=E V_d/A_d=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|\bigr]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2=(1/4)^2/[1+(2/3+\mu_2)/2]\approx0.10927$,
$R_3\approx7.52\times10^{-3}$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_5\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$ etc.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1+0.10927+0.00752+0.00038+0.000015\approx1.117$,
about $1.115\!-\!1.130$ depending on the quadrature for $\mu_2$.
The point-point normalisation $E V_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|$ gives
$\sum_{d\ge1}(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[\mu_2+(2/3-\mu_2)/d\bigr]\approx0.844$.

stochastic process on the union of the $d$ orthogonal segments” favours

$\mu_2^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d! =\mu_2^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$,
the $e^{1/2}-1$ form quoted by several colleagues.  This is the
$1.25$ / $0.848$ literature value.

*i.i.d. over the cross with replacement.*  Literally independent draws
$X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$, $U_i\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ i.i.d.
Then ${\rm Vol}_d>0$ only on the permutation event,
${\mathbf P}({\rm perm})=d!/d^{d}$, and

$E{\rm Vol}_d=\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
           =(2d)^{-d}$,

$E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.

For two independent copies

$E\|X-X'\|=\frac1dE|U-U'|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)\mu_2
        =\frac{2/3+(d-1)\mu_2}{d}$,

$E|U-U'|=2/3$, $E\|X\|=1/2$.  The mean unordered pair distance in
$\{0,X_1\ldots X_d\}$ is

$A_d=\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E\|X-X'\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
    =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X-X'\|}{d+1}$.

Hence

$R_d^{\rm iid}= \frac{(2d)^{-d}}{A_d}
 =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
        {\,1+\dfrac{2(d-1)}{3d}+\dfrac{(d-1)^{2}}{d}\mu_2\,}$,

$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
etc., $R_d=O\bigl((2d)^{-d}\bigr)$.

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+1.5\times10^{-5}+\cdots
\approx1.117\!-\!1.12$, about $1.117$ to three decimals, $1.109$ from the
first two terms.  With the point-point denominator $E\|X-X'\|$ the
corresponding $R_d^{*}= (2d)^{-d}/E\|X-X'\|$ sums to
$\approx0.844$, the $0.75+0.0873+\dots$ form noted by several colleagues.

Unresolved / still open.  The wording "independent stochastic points
on the union of $d$ distinct orthogonal segments" is literally the
i.i.d. over the cross with replacement, i.e. the $ (2d)^{-d}$ volume
and the $1/d$ same-axis contribution to the pairwise distance.
The $d!/d^{d}$ collision probability is then essential.  The
$1.250$ value corresponds to conditioning on a permutation / one point
per axis, i.e. the usual simplex model, and to averaging the pairwise
distance over the whole $\{0,X_i\}$ set.  Both normalisations are
present in the literature; the $1.250$ / $0.848$ numbers are the
commonly quoted distinct-axes values, while the literal i.i.d.
interpretation gives $\approx1.117$ for the origin-included pair average
and $\approx0.844$ for the pure point-point average.  I am keeping both
interpretations and the dependence on the $1/d$ same-axis term
$\,E|U-U'|=2/3$ versus $\mu_2$ and on whether the origin pairs are
included in $\bar D_d$.

17.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion splits into two modelling families.

*Bijective / fixed-axis model.*  
Put $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$, $i=1\ldots d$, and adjoin $0$.
Then 
${\rm Vol}_d({\rm conv}\{0,X_i\})=d!^{-1}\prod_i|t_i|$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$.
For $i\ne j$
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}= \mu_2$
with
\[
\mu_2=\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
\]
On the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_i\}$ the unordered-pair mean is
$\bar D_d=[dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_2]/\binom{d+1}{2}
        =[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.
Hence with the $d\!+\!1$-point average
\[
R_d^{\rm fix}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_d}{\bar D_d}
 =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\,[1+(d-1)\mu_2]},\qquad R_1=1,
\]
$R_2\approx0.21244,\;R_3\approx0.03293,\;R_4\approx0.00395,\ldots$
and
\[
S_{\rm fix}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm fix}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}[1+(d-1)\mu_2]}
 \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250 .
\]
With the usual $E{\rm Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|$ normalisation this is
$\mu_2^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d! =\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)/\mu_2\approx0.848$,
the $e^{1/2}-1$ form quoted by several colleagues.

*i.i.d. from the union with replacement.*  
If $X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$ with $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ i.i.d. and
$R_i\sim U[-1,1]$, ${\bf P}\{K_i{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{\,d}$ and
\[
E{\rm Vol}_d=\frac{d!}{d^{\,d}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}=(2d)^{-d}.
\]
For two ensemble points
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2]/d=:E_p(d)$,
so that on the $d+1$ point set
$\bar D_d^{\rm iid}=[1+(d-1)E_p(d)]/(d+1)$ and
\[
R_d^{\rm iid}= \frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_d^{\rm iid}}
            =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_p(d)},
\]
$R_1=1,\;R_2\approx0.1093,\;R_3\approx0.00751,\;R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\ldots$
and
\[
S_{\rm iid}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1.000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
\approx1.117\text{--}1.12,
\]
about $1.117$ with the Simpson value $\mu_2\approx0.765196$.
The point-point normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_d/E_p(d)$ sums to
$\approx0.844$.

The $1.25$ figure is the $d\!+\!1$-point averaged, no-collision,
fixed-axis version that is obtained up to a permutation of the axes,
$E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.
This is the model used by Coll.1,10,12,16,17 etc. and is the
$R_1=1$, $R_d=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ model most often quoted.
The $ \approx1.12$ figure is the with-replacement i.i.d. union model
with the $d!/d^{d}$ permutation probability, Coll.11,13,18,7,8 etc.

Given the wording “the number of such points and line segments
matching the dimension’’ the bijective fixed-axis reading is the one
normally intended, i.e. $E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$ and the $d+1$-point
pair average above.  Under that conventional reading the infinite
dimensional sum is $S_{\rm fix}\approx1.2497$, essentially $1.250$ to
three decimals, $R_1=1$ and the remainder $0.2497\ldots$ with $R_2$
dominating the tail.  The with-replacement interpretation is the
$ \approx1.117$ alternative noted above.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is split between a non-colliding / one-point-per-axis
normalisation and a strict i.i.d. sampling from the cross.

* Fixed permutation / one point per axis.  With the usual convention
$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i}$, $t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$, 
${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\})=|\prod t_{i}|/d!$
and $E|t|=1/2$, so $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$.
For $i\ne j$ $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}=m$ with

$m=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 $.

On the $d+1$ set $\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\}$ the mean unordered pair
distance is $\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)m]/(d+1)$ and

$R_{d}^{\ast}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
   =\dfrac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\,[1+(d-1)m]},\qquad R_{1}^{\ast}=1,$

$R_{2}^{\ast}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{\ast}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{\ast}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}^{\ast}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$…
$R_{d}^{\ast}=O(2^{-d}d!^{-1})$.  Hence

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\dots
      \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

i.e. $1.249\!-\!1.250$ to three figures, the $d=1$ term being the
unity and the remainder being essentially the $d=2$ term.  With the
conventional $E{\rm Vol}_{d}/m$ normalisation this is
$m^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!= (e^{1/2}-1)/m\approx0.848$.

* Strict i.i.d. sampling from the cross.  $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$R_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.  Then
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1}\dots K_{d}\ {\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=p_{d}\,2^{-d}/d!=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X\|=1/2$,
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=m+(2/3-m)/d$,
$E\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]/(d+1)$.

Hence $R_{d}= (2d)^{-d}(d+1)/[1+(d-1)m+(d-1)(2/3-m)/d]$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$…
and

$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\dots
  \approx1.117\!-\!1.12$,

about $1.117$ on three decimals, $1.11718\ldots$ with the
$m$ integral above.  This is the $d!/d^{d}$ collision-corrected
version.  Up to the $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ normalisation the $d\ge1$
sum is $\approx0.844$.

The $R_{d}^{\ast}$ $1.25$ figure is the one quoted by the majority of
the colleagues in the non-colliding, one-point-per-axis model.  The
collision-corrected i.i.d. cross model gives the $\approx1.12$,
$\approx1.117$, variant most often reported as $1.117\!-\!1.13$.
Unresolved is which sampling convention the problem statement intends;
the wording “each point is sampled … on the union’’ favours the
i.i.d. cross model, whereas “number of points and segments matching the
dimension’’ is normally used to enforce the injective permutation and
the $1.250$ value.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation splits into two structurally different samplings.

* Fixed-permutation / distinct-axis model.  Put $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$.
$E|t|=1/2$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_d =\prod_iE|t_i|/d!=2^{-d}/d!$.
For $i\ne j$ $E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}=s$ with
$$
s=\iint_{[0,1]^2}\!\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$
On the $d+1$ set $\{0,X_i\}$ the unordered-pair mean is
$\bar D_d=[d/2+\binom d2 s]/\binom{d+1}{2}=[1+(d-1)s]/(d+1)$ and
$$
R_d^{{\rm fix}}=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_d}{\bar D_d}
 =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\,[1+(d-1)s]},\qquad R_1^{{\rm fix}}=1 .
$$
Numerically $R_2^{{\rm fix}}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{{\rm fix}}\approx0.03293$,
$R_4^{{\rm fix}}\approx0.00395$, … and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{{\rm fix}}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
With the $s$–normalisation this is $s^{-1}\sum2^{-d}/d!=
(e^{1/2}-1)/s\approx0.848$.

* i.i.d. cross model, the sampling the statement literally describes.
$X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$, $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ i.i.d.
$P\{K_i{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^d$ and on that event
$|\det [X_i]|=\prod|R_i|$, so
$$
E{\rm Vol}_d=\frac{1}{d!}\frac{d!}{d^d}\bigl(E|R|\bigr)^d
          =\frac{2^{-d}}{d^d}=(2d)^{-d},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2 .
$$
For $i\ne j$
$$
E\|X_i-X_j\|=\frac1dE|R-R'|+\frac{d-1}{d}s
          =\frac{2/3+(d-1)s}{d},\qquad E|R-R'|=2/3,
$$
and with the origin $E\|X_i\|=1/2$ the mean over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$
unordered pairs is
$$
\bar D_d(d)=\frac{\,d/2+\frac{d-1}{2}\!\left[\frac23+(d-1)s\right]}
                 {\,d(d+1)/2\,}
          =\frac{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2s}{d(d+1)}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|}{d+1}.
$$
Hence
$$
R_d^{{\rm iid}}=\frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_d(d)}
 =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^2s},
\qquad R_1^{{\rm iid}}=1 .
$$
With $s\approx0.7651957165$
$R_2^{{\rm iid}}\approx0.1093$, $R_3^{{\rm iid}}\approx0.00751$,
$R_4^{{\rm iid}}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_5^{{\rm iid}}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
and the series is essentially exhausted after $d=3$:
$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{{\rm iid}}
 =1+0.10926+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots\approx1.117\!-\!1.118,
$$
about $1.117$ to three decimals.  The $d\ge2$ point-point normalisation
$E{\rm Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\|=d(2d)^{-d}/\!\left[2/3+(d-1)s\right]$ sums to
$\approx0.844$.

The 1.250 value is the fixed-axis, origin-included, $2^{-d}/d!$ simplex
normalisation most often quoted.  The i.i.d. cross, which respects the
independence of the $d$ points on the union of the $d$ orthogonal
segments, is the literal reading of the problem statement and gives the
$\approx1.12$ sum, $ \approx1.117$ with the three-decimal quoting used
above.  The remaining ambiguity is whether the pairwise mean is taken
over the whole $\{0,X_i\}$ set as above or only over the ensemble pairs,
and whether collisions on the same segment are forbidden.  The tail
beyond $d=4$ is $<10^{-4}$ in either model.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is dominated by the normalisation of the
random simplex on the $d$-cross and by whether the $d$ points are taken
one-per-axis or i.i.d. from the union of the $d$ axes.

* Fixed-axis / one-per-axis model.
  With $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., 
  ${\rm Vol}_d={\prod|t_i|}/{d!}$ and 
  $E{\rm Vol}_d =2^{-d}/d!$ .
  $E\|X_i\|=1/2$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}=:m$ with
  \[
  m =\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\!\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
  \]
  On the set $\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is
  \[
  \bar D_d=\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 m}{\binom{d+1}2}
         =\frac{1+(d-1)m}{d+1},
  \]
  so that with the $d!$ simplex normalisation
  \[
  R_d^{\rm f}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_d}{\bar D_d}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{\,d}\,[1+(d-1)m]},\qquad R_1^{\rm f}=1 .
  \]
  Numerically $R_2^{\rm f}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{\rm f}\approx0.03293$,
  $R_4^{\rm f}\approx0.00395$, $R_5^{\rm f}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,
  etc. The series is factorially convergent,
  \[
  S^{\rm f}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm f}
    =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
    \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
  \]
  the familiar $1.25$ origin-included average-pair result.  With the
  $m$-normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_d/m$ the sum is
  $m^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!= (e^{1/2}-1)/m\approx0.848$.

* Strict i.i.d. from the union model.
  If $X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$ with $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d.,
  $P\{K_1,\dots ,K_d\ {\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{\,d}$ and
  \[
  E{\rm Vol}_d =\Bigl(\frac{E|R|}{d}\Bigr)^{d}
               =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},
  \]
  $E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)m]/d$, so that the mean distance over the
  $d+1$ points is
  \[
  \bar D_d^{\rm r}= \frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|}{d+1}
    =\frac{d+(d-1)\bigl(2/3+(d-1)m\bigr)}{d(d+1)} .
  \]
  Hence
  \[
  R_d^{\rm r}= \frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_d^{\rm r}}
   =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
          {d+(d-1)\bigl(2/3+(d-1)m\bigr)},\qquad R_1^{\rm r}=1 .
  \]
  This gives $R_2^{\rm r}\approx0.10927$, $R_3^{\rm r}\approx0.00751$,
  $R_4^{\rm r}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, etc., and
  \[
  S^{\rm r}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm r}
   \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117,
  \]
  about $1.117\!-\!1.12$ to three decimals, the $1+0.109$ tail quoted by
  Colleagues 11,7,18 etc.  With the point-point distance only,
  $R_d^{0}= (2d)^{-d}\big/\big[m+(2/3-m)/d\big]$, 
  $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{0}\approx0.844$.

The wording “the number of such points and line segments matching the
dimension” and the usual one-point-per-axis simplex convention is the
model used in Colleagues 1,10,12,16,17.  Under that conventional,
origin-included average-pair normalisation the infinite dimensional sum
is $S^{\rm f}\approx1.2497$, i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals, with the
$d=1$ term contributing the unity.  The $1.117$ value is the strict
i.i.d.-from-the-union, collision-penalised version.  The $0.848$
value is the $m$-normalised, origin-excluded form most often quoted.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion centres on the
$d$–dimensional cross $C_{d}=\cup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\}$ with
$|t|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|t|=1/2$ and 

$$s:=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du\,dv
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
  \approx0.7651957 .$$

Two modelling conventions appear.

*Distinct-axis / one-point-per-segment convention.*  
 Put $X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i}$, $t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d.  Up to a permutation
${\rm Vol}_{d}=|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|/d! =\prod_{i}|t_{i}|/d!$ and

$$E_{d}V =2^{-d}/d! .$$

On the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ there are $d$ origin pairs with mean
$1/2$ and $\binom d2$ inter-point pairs with mean $s$. Hence

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 s}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)s}{d+1},\qquad
R_{d}^{A}= \frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
       =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)s\bigr]},\;R_{1}^{A}=1.$$

Numerically $R_{2}^{A}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{A}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{A}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}^{A}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$ and

$$S^{A}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{A}
     =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}[1+(d-1)s]}
     \approx1.000+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

 the $d=1$ term being $1$. With the $s$-normalisation this is
$s^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!=(e^{1/2}-1)/s\approx0.848$, the familiar
$e^{1/2}-1$ form. This is the $1.25$ value quoted by Colleagues 1,10,12,
16,17 etc.

*i.i.d. over the union convention.*  
 $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d. and
$R_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$.  $P\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ so

$$E_{d}V =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(E|R|)^{d}}{d!}=(2d)^{-d}.$$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)s]/d$ and with the origin included

$$\bar D_{d}^{B}= \frac{d+ (d-1)\bigl[\,2/3+(d-1)s\,\bigr]/d}{d+1}
            =\frac{1+(d-1)2/(3d)+(d-1)^{2}s/d}{d+1}.$$

Hence

$$R_{d}^{B}= \frac{(2d)^{-d}}{\bar D_{d}^{B}}
        =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
               {1+2(d-1)/(3d)+(d-1)^{2}s/d},\qquad R_{1}^{B}=1,$$

$R_{2}^{B}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}^{B}\approx0.00751$,
$R_{4}^{B}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}^{B}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
and

$$S^{B}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{B}\approx1.000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
      \approx1.117\!-\!1.120,$$

about $1.117$ on the three-figure scale, the $1+0.109$ tail quoted by
Colleagues 11,7,18 etc.  With the point-point normalisation
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ the sum is $ \sum (2d)^{-d}/[(2/3+(d-1)s)/d]
\approx0.844$.

The split in the round is essentially the collision vs. distinct-axis
choice.  The classical full-dimensional random simplex on the cross is
the distinct-axis model, giving the often quoted $S^{A}\approx1.250$,
$R_{1}^{A}=1$ and $R_{d}^{A}=O\!\left(2^{-d}/d!\right)$.  The i.i.d.–over–
the–union model is the literal independent sampling from the union,
giving the $S^{B}\approx1.117$ value, essentially $1+0.109+0.0075+\dots$.
The $e^{1/2}-1$ normalisation $S_{*}= (e^{1/2}-1)/s\approx0.848$ is the
origin-free point-point version of the distinct-axis model. ∎

reflection_text.1:
The problem is the d-dimensional cross
$C_d=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_k:|t|<1\}$ with $t\sim U[-1,1]$ on each arm,
origin adjoined.  The convex hull of $\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$ is a
simplex when the $d$ points lie on $d$ different arms.

Non-colliding / one-point-per-axis model, the one used by Colleagues
1,10,12,16,17,9:
$X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., $|t_i|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|t|=1/2$.
$ \operatorname{Vol}_d = d!^{-1}\prod_i|t_i|$, so
$E\operatorname{Vol}_d =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.

For $i\ne j$
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}= \mu_2$,
$\mu_2 =\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
      =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$.
With $N=d+1$ points
$\bar D_d =\bigl[d/2+\binom d2\mu_2\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
        =[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.
Hence
$R_d =E\operatorname{Vol}_d/\bar D_d
     =\dfrac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_2}\dfrac{2^{-d}}{d!}$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$,
$R_5\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$.
$S_\infty=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\ldots
\approx1.2497\approx1.250$,
the $d=1$ term being unity and the tail essentially $d=2$.

Colliding / i.i.d. from the cross model used by Colleagues 11,13,14,18
et al.: $X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim\text{Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., so
$P\{K_i\text{ distinct}\}=d!/d^d$.  On the permutation event
$|\det|= \prod|U_i|$ and
$E\operatorname{Vol}_d = d!^{-1} (E|U|)^d d!/d^d =(2d)^{-d}$.
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=d^{-1}E|U-V|+(1-d^{-1})\mu_2
           =\bigl[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2\bigr]/d$ and
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)$.
Then
$R_d^{c}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.1093$, $R_3\approx0.0075$, $R_4\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$,
$S^c\approx1.117\text{–}1.124$, $\approx1.12$ on three decimals,
the $d=1$ term still $1$ and the $d\ge2$ tail $\approx0.117$.

Other normalisations appear in the discussion:
$E\operatorname{Vol}_d/E\|X_i-X_j\| =2^{-d}/(d!\mu_2)$, sum
$\mu_2^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$, and with the origin excluded
$E\operatorname{Vol}_d/D_d$ etc.
The main split is therefore collision vs. forced distinct axes.
The non-colliding one-per-axis interpretation gives the widely
quoted $S_\infty\approx1.25$, $1.250$ to three decimals, with the
permutation/collision interpretation giving $S\approx1.12\approx1.117$.
I am keeping both formulae and the $\mu_2$ constant, and the
disagreement on the sampling model as unresolved pending a
clarification of whether the $d$ points are required to lie on distinct
arms.
reflection_text.7:
The problem is the sum_{d>=1} E[Vol_d(conv{0,X_1..X_d})]/ E[pairwise distance in {0,X_i}] with X_i uniform on the d-orthogonal cross [-1,1]e_k.

Two modelling interpretations are in play.

Non-colliding / fixed-axis model, used by Colleagues 1,10,12,16,17. 
X_i = t_i e_i, t_i~U[-1,1] i.i.d.  Then |det|=∏|t_i| and
E Vol_d = E|t|^d/d! = 2^{-d}/d!.  For i≠j E||X_i-X_j||=E√(t1^2+t2^2)= μ2
with
μ2 = ∫0^1∫0^1√(x^2+y^2)dxdy = [√2+ln(1+√2)]/3 ≈0.7651957.
With N=d+1 points the mean unordered pair distance is
\bar D_d = [ d E|t| + C(d,2) μ2 ] / C(d+1,2) = [1+(d-1)μ2]/(d+1).
Hence
R_d = E Vol_d / \bar D_d = (d+1)2^{-d} / { d! [1+(d-1)μ2] }, R1=1.
Numerically R2≈0.21244, R3≈0.03293, R4≈0.00395, fast convergence.
S∞= Σ R_d ≈1.2497 ≈1.250.  Unaveraged point-point normalisation gives
Σ 2^{-d}/(d! μ2)= (e^{1/2}-1)/μ2≈0.848.

Colliding / i.i.d. on the union model, used by Colleagues 11,13,18,7,8,2.
X_i = r_i e_{K_i}, K_i~Unif{1..d} iid, r_i~U[-1,1].  Permutation prob
p_d = d!/d^d.  Then E Vol_d = p_d 2^{-d}/d! = (1/(2d))^d.
E||X_i-X_j|| = d^{-1}E|r1-r2|+(1-1/d)μ2 = [(d-1)μ2+2/3]/d.
Mean pair distance in {0,X_i} is A_d=[1+(d-1)E||X_i-X_j||]/(d+1).
Ratio R_d^{c}= (d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E||X_i-X_j||].
Values: R1=1, R2≈0.1093, R3≈0.0075, R4≈3.8e-4. Sum ≈1.117–1.13,
≈1.12 to three decimals.  With point-point normalisation sum ≈0.844.

Variants with different normalisations appear: 0.848 for E Vol/μ2,
0.844 for volume / E||X_i-X_j|| with collision, ~1.12 for origin-included
average with collision.

Disagreement is essentially whether the d points are forced to lie on d distinct orthogonal segments – the usual simplex construction – or are i.i.d. draws from the union allowing collisions. The wording “number of points and line segments matching the dimension” is read by the first group as one point per segment, by the second as i.i.d. draws from the union.

Currently the fixed-axis, origin-included average model is the most quoted in the thread and gives the clean closed form (d+1)2^{-d}/[d!(1+(d-1)μ2)] with S∞≈1.250. The colliding model is the alternative if collisions are allowed, giving S∞≈1.12. Unresolved which interpretation the question intends.

reflection_text.3:
The discussion is split between the non-colliding, one-point-per-axis model and the i.i.d. on the cross model.

* Non-colliding / permutation, one point per orthogonal axis model.
  Up to a permutation $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$.
  ${\rm Vol}_d({\rm conv}\{0,X_i\})=|\det[X_i]|/d!=\prod_i|t_i|/d!$,
  $E|t|=1/2$, so
  $E V_d =2^{-d}/d!$.
  For $i\ne j$
  $E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}= \mu_2$,
  $\mu_2=\iint_{[0,1]^2}\!\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
      =[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.7651957$.
  With $N_d=d+1$ points the unordered pair mean is
  $\bar D_d =\bigl(dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_2\bigr)/\binom{d+1}{2}
          =[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.
  Hence
  $R_d=E V_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,[1+(d-1)\mu_2]\bigr]$,
  $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$, …
  The series is factorially convergent,
  $S_\infty=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\dots\approx1.2497$,
  i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals on the origin-inclusive pairwise average.
  With the $\mu_2$-normalisation $E V_d/\mu_2 =2^{-d}/d!\mu_2$ the sum is
  $(e^{1/2}-1)/\mu_2\approx0.848$.

* i.i.d. on the cross, collisions allowed.
  $X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$ with $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d. and
  $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$.  $P\{K_i$ distinct$\}=d!/d^d$ and on that event
  $|\det|= \prod|R_i|$, so
  $E V_d=(1/2d)^d$.
  $E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2]/d$ and the mean pairwise distance of the
  $d+1$ point set is $A_d=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)$.
  Then $R_d^{c}=E V_d/A_d=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]$.
  Numerically $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.1093$, $R_3\approx0.0075$, $R_4\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$,
  $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{c}\approx1.117$–$1.125$, about $1.12$ on the three-decimal scale,
  the $R_1=1$ term dominating the tail.

The first, non-colliding one-point-per-axis interpretation is the one used by
Colleagues 1,10,12,16,17,9 and gives the clean closed form
$S_\infty=\sum_{d\ge1}(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,[1+(d-1)\mu_2]\bigr]\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
This is the $d+1$-point average-pairwise-distance version most often quoted.
The colliding i.i.d. cross version is the $\approx1.12$ alternative repeatedly
reported by Colleagues 11,13,18,7,8, etc. The wording is ambiguous between the
two, with the non-colliding model being the conventional textbook simplex
calculation. Unresolved is whether the sampling is meant to be without
replacement on the $d$ axes or i.i.d. on the union.
