$s^{-1}\sum 2^{-d}/d!=(e^{1/2}-1)/s\approx0.848$.  This is the $1.25$ value quoted by the majority in round 1: Colleagues 1,10,12,13,14,16,17,18,2,3,5,7,8,9.

*I.i.d. over the union convention – independent draws from $C_{d}$ with possible collisions.*

$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.  $P\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$.

$E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)s]/d\equiv E_{p}(d)$,
$\bar D_{d}^{B}=[1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)]/(d+1)$.

$R_{d}^{B}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)\bigr]$, $R_{1}^{B}=1$,

$R_{2}^{B}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}^{B}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}^{B}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$.

$S^{B}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{B}\approx1.000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117\!-\!1.120$, about $1.117$.

This is the $ \approx1.12$ minority reading: Colleagues 11,7,10 remark,15,16,4,6.

Disagreement is interpretational: “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” + “number of points and line segments matching the dimension” is read by the majority as a bijection/one point per segment, i.e. the non-colliding simplex with $E V=2^{-d}/d!$ and the $1.250$ sum; the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor and the $(2d)^{-d}$ volume are read as sampling-with-replacement from the union, giving $\approx1.117$.

Fixed-axis / one-per-axis, non-colliding, origin-inclusive model – the reading favoured by the wording “d distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … number of points and line segments matching the dimension”. 
With $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., $E|t|=1/2$,

$E{\rm Vol}_d =2^{-d}/d!$,

$\mu_2=E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}

       =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_2}{d+1}$,

$R_d^{f}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d
       =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}[1+(d-1)\mu_2]},\;R_1^{f}=1$,

$R_2^{f}\approx0.21244,\;R_3^{f}\approx0.03293,\;R_4^{f}\approx0.00395,\dots$

to three decimals.  The $\mu_2$-normalised point-point sum is

for $E{\rm Vol}_d/\mu_2$.

$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2]/d$,
$\bar D_d^{r}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)$,

Current round public output is dominated by the fixed-axis interpretation,

Unresolved: the precise intended sampling semantics of “ensemble of independent stochastic points” on the union of $d$ distinct segments with matching cardinalities.  Under the literal distinct-segment bijection the conventional textbook answer is $S\approx1.250$, $R_1=1$, $m\approx0.765196$.  The $1.117$ value is the i.i.d.-with-replacement, permutation-probability-adjusted variant.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation is split between two sampling conventions for the d points on the d orthogonal segments.

*Fixed-axes / bijection / permutation-fixed model.*  
Put $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., origin adjoined.  Up to relabelling the axes are distinct by construction.  
$E V_d =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=\mu_2$ with 
$\mu_2=\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
      =[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.7651957$.  
Mean unordered pair distance on $\{0,X_i\}$:
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.  
$R_d^{\rm fix}=E V_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,(1+(d-1)\mu_2)\bigr]$, $R_1=1$, 
$R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm fix}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
Point-point normalisation $E V_d/\mu_2$ gives $\mu_2^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$.

This is the model used by Colleagues 1,8,9,10,12,13,14,16,17,18 and argued as the literal reading of “$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” and “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”, i.e. a bijection points↔segments, no replacement, $P\{{\rm perm}\}=1$, $|\det|>0$ a.s.  The $d!/d^d$ collision factor is then an artefact of sampling with replacement.

*I.i.d. axis / with-replacement model.*  
$X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$, $U_i\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.  
$P\{K_i{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^d$, on that event $|\det|=\prod|U_i|$, so
$E V_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E_1V=1/2$.  
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2]/d$, mean unordered pair distance
$\bar D_d=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)$,
$R_d^{\rm iid}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79e-4$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1.117\!-\!1.12$, about $1.117$ with Simpson
$\mu_2$.  Point-point normalisation gives $\sum(2d)^{-d}/E\|X_i-X_j\|\approx0.844$.

Colleagues 11,15,4,7 etc give this $1.12\!-\!1.13$ value and note the
$0.844/0.848$ point-point variants.  The wording “ensemble of independent
stochastic points” and “uniform stochastic process on the union” favours
this with-replacement reading.

Current round consensus is heavily toward the bijection interpretation,
with many colleagues explicitly rejecting the $d!/d^d$ factor as a
misreading of “distinct”.  The $1.250$ origin-inclusive average-pair sum
and the $0.848$ $\mu_2$-normalised sum are the numbers repeatedly quoted
for the fixed-axes model, while the $1.117\approx1.12$ sum is the
collision-penalised i.i.d.-on-the-union variant.  Unresolved is whether
“independent stochastic points on the union” should be read as i.i.d.
with replacement or as a bijection enforced by the statement that the
numbers of points and segments match.  The residual uncertainty is exactly
the dependence/independence of the axis choice and the definition of the
mean pairwise distance – over the $d+1$ set including the origin versus
between two independent points only.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The current round re-states the two competing normalisations that were already in the previous reflection.

* Fixed-axis / non-colliding, one point per orthogonal axis, bijection point↔segment.
Up to permutation $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$, $|t_i|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|t|=1/2$.
${\rm Vol}_d({\rm conv}\{0,X_i\})=|\det[X_i]|/d!=\prod|t_i|/d!$ so
$E V_d =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.
For $i\ne j$ $E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}=:\mu_2$
$\mu_2=\iint_{[0,1]^2}\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
      =[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.7651957$.
With $N_d=d+1$ points the unordered-pair mean is
$\bar D_d=[dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_2]/\binom{d+1}{2}=[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.
Hence $R_d^{fix}=E V_d/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,[1+(d-1)\mu_2]\bigr]$,
$R_1=1$, $R_2=3/[8(1+\mu_2)]\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$.
$S^{fix}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{fix}\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
$\mu_2$-normalised form $\sum2^{-d}/d!/\mu_2=(e^{1/2}-1)/\mu_2\approx0.848$.

This is the model used by Colleagues 1,10,12,13,14,17,18,2,3,5,7,8,9 and is
exactly the $d!$-normalised orthogonal simplex with the one-point-per-axis
bijection implied by “distinct mutually orthogonal segments’’ and “the number
of points and line segments matching the dimension’’.

* i.i.d. on the union of the $d$ segments, collisions allowed.
$X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ i.i.d., $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$.
$P\{K_i$ distinct$\}=d!/d^d$, on the permutation event $|\det|=\prod|R_i|$.
$E V_d^{c}=(2d)^{-d}$.
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2]/d=:E_p(d)$.
Origin-inclusive pair mean $\bar D_d^{c}=[1+(d-1)E_p(d)]/(d+1)$.
$R_d^{c}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E_p(d)]$, $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$,
$R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.8\times10^{-4}$.
$S^{c}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.117\approx1.12$.
Point–point normalisation gives $\sum(2d)^{-d}/E_p(d)\approx0.844$.

The current round still shows the split.  Most colleagues argue that the
wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ together with the
matching number of points and segments enforces a bijection, i.e. no

  =[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]/(d+1)$.  Hence
  $R_{d}^{\rm f}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
   =\dfrac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\dfrac{2^{-d}}{d!}$,
  $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
  $R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$.
  $S^{\rm f}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm f}\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots
  \approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
  The $\mu_{2}$-normalised form is $\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!
  =\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$.  This is the value quoted by
  Colleagues 1,10,12,13,14,16,17,18,2,3,5,7,8,9.

* Colliding / i.i.d. from the union model.
  $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $U_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$
  i.i.d.  $P\{K_{1..d}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$.
  On the permutation event $|\det|=\prod|U_{i}|$, so
  $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!^{-1}E|U|^{d}d!/d^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$.
  $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}E|U-V|+(1-d^{-1})\mu_{2}
  =[2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}]/d=:E_{p}(d)$.
  Origin-inclusive mean pair distance
  $\bar D_{d}^{c}=[1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)]/(d+1)$.
  $R_{d}^{c}= (d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)]$,
  $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$,
  $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$.
  $S^{c}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{c}\approx1.000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
  \approx1.117\approx1.12$, about $1.117\!-\!1.124$ depending on quadrature.
  Point-point normalised sum is $\sum(2d)^{-d}/E_{p}(d)\approx0.844$.

The split is the $d!/d^{d}$ permutation factor and the mixed same-axis
distance $E|U-V|=2/3$.  The injective reading conditions on a bijection
points↔segments, removing the zero-volume mass and giving $E{\rm Vol}_{d}
=2^{-d}/d!$.  The i.i.d. reading keeps the $d!/d^{d}$ probability of a
full-dimensional simplex and gives $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$.

The wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ and
“the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’
is used by Colleagues 13,14,5,8,9 to argue for the injective one-point-per-
segment bijection, i.e. the $S\approx1.250$ value with $R_{1}=1$.  Colleagues
11,15,16,10,4,6,7, etc. keep the i.i.d. on the union interpretation,
giving $S\approx1.117\approx1.12$ with $R_{1}=1$.

Constants are stable: $\mu_{2}=[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.765196$,
$E|t|=1/2$, $E|U-V|=2/3$.  $R_{d}=O(2^{-d}d!^{-1})$ in the injective
model and $O((2d)^{-d})$ in the colliding model, so both series are
essentially exhausted by $d=2\!-\!3$.  Unresolved is whether the intended
sampling is the forced distinct-arm bijection or i.i.d. sampling from
the union with possible collisions.  I am retaining both closed forms
and the numerical summaries $S^{\rm f}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$ and
$S^{c}\approx1.117\approx1.12$, with the non-colliding $1.250$ being the
text-book one-point-per-axis, origin-inclusive pairwise-average
normalisation most often quoted.
reflection_text.16:
The discussion remains split between the textbook one-point-per-axis / bijection model and the literal i.i.d. draw from the union of the $d$ orthogonal segments with replacement.

Distinct-axes / injective model, the dominant public reading in round 1:

* $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., $|t|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|t|=1/2$.
* Up to permutation ${\rm Vol}_d({\rm conv}\{0,X_i\})=d!^{-1}\prod_i|t_i|$.
* $E{\rm Vol}_d =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.
* For $i\neq j$, $\mu_2:=E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
   =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$.
* On the $d+1$ point set $\{0,X_i\}$, mean unordered pair distance
  $\bar D_d=\bigl[d/2+\binom d2\mu_2\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
          =\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_2\bigr]/(d+1)$.
* $R_d^{\rm fix}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d
   =(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl\{d![1+(d-1)\mu_2]\bigr\}$, $R_1=1$.
  $R_2\approx0.21244$, $R_3\approx0.03293$, $R_4\approx0.00395$, $R_5\approx3.85e-4$.
* $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm fix}\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\ldots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
  $\mu_2$-normalised point-point form is $\mu_2^{-1}\sum2^{-d}/d!
   =\mu_2^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$, i.e. the $e^{1/2}-1$ literature value.

The i.i.d. over the cross with replacement model, the literal “uniform on the union’’ reading:

* $X_i=U_i e_{K_i}$, $U_i\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.
* ${\rm P}\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^d$, $E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$, $E{\rm Vol}_1=1/2$.
* $E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2]/d$, $E|U-U'|=2/3$.
* Origin-inclusive mean pair distance
  $A_d=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)
      =[1+2(d-1)/3d+(d-1)^2\mu_2/d]/(d+1)$.
* $R_d^{\rm iid}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]$.
  $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79e-4$.
* $\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{\rm iid}\approx1.000+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\ldots
   \approx1.117\!-\!1.12$, $\approx1.117$ to three decimals.
  Point-point normalisation gives $\sum(2d)^{-d}/E\|X_i-X_j\|\approx0.844$.

Round 1 public votes: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,14,16,17,18,2,3,5,7,8,9 argue the wording “$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal segments … number of points and segments matching the dimension’’ is the bijection / one-point-per-segment convention, the $d!/d^d$ collision penalty is not intended, and the correct sum is the $1.250$ origin-inclusive value, with the $0.848$ $\mu_2$-normalised form.

reflection_text.18:
The model is the origin-augmented orthogonal cross simplex.  
With the textbook one-point-per-axis, non-colliding interpretation which is
the literal reading of “d distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’
and “the number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’,
up to relabelling $X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$, $|t_i|\sim U[0,1]$,
$E|t|=1/2$.

$ {\rm Vol}_d({\rm conv}\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\})=
|\det[X_1\ldots X_d]|/d!=\prod_i|t_i|/d! $,
$E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$.

For $i\ne j$ on orthogonal axes
$\mu_2:=E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}
 =\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
 =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.7651957$.

With $N_d=d+1$ points the origin-inclusive mean unordered pair distance is
$\bar D_d=[dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_2]/\binom{d+1}{2}
=[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.
Hence
$R_d^{fix}=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d
 =(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl\{d![1+(d-1)\mu_2]\bigr\}$,
$R_1^{fix}=1$, $R_2^{fix}=3/[8(1+\mu_2)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_3^{fix}\approx0.03293$, $R_4^{fix}\approx0.00395$, $R_5^{fix}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,
$R_d=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.  
$S_{fix}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{fix}=1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\dots\approx1.2497\approx1.250$
three-decimal.  The $\mu_2$-normalised $E{\rm Vol}_d/\mu_2$ sum is
$\mu_2^{-1}\sum2^{-d}/d!=(e^{1/2}-1)/\mu_2\approx0.848$.

The alternative i.i.d. on the union reading $X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$,
$K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., gives $P\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(2d)^{-d}$.  Then $E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2]/d$,
$\bar D_d^{rand}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]/(d+1)$ and
$R_d^{rand}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_i-X_j\|]$,
$R_1^{rand}=1$, $R_2^{rand}\approx0.1093$, $R_3^{rand}\approx0.0075$,
$S^{rand}\approx1.117\!-\!1.13$, ~1.117 to three decimals, with
point-point normalisation $\sum(2d)^{-d}/E\|X_i-X_j\|\approx0.844$.

Round-1 public discussion is dominated by the fixed-axis, bijection
interpretation giving $S\approx1.25$, $R_1=1$, $R_2\approx0.212$ and
essentially all mass in $d=1,2$.  The $~1.12$ family is the with-replacement
i.i.d. cross model with the $d!/d^d$ collision penalty. The wording

favours the bijection/non-colliding $2^{-d}/d!$ model, i.e. the $1.250$

random-axis with-replacement reading. Unresolved is which sampling

on the union’’.

1.text:
The $d+1$ point set is ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and, up to a
permutation of the $d$ orthogonal axes, the distinct–segment, one-point-
per-segment realisation can be written

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1],\qquad 
|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2,$$

i.i.d.  On the full–dimensional realisation

${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\bigr)=
d!^{-1}\bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|
=d!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|$,

so that with the usual $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$E_{d}{\rm Vol}=d!^{-1}\bigl(E|t|\bigr)^{d}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,$$

and for $i\ne j$ on two different axes

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957,$$

independent of $d$.  The $d+1$ points have $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered
pairs, $d$ of them $0\!-\!X_{i}$ and $\binom d2$ inter–point pairs, hence
the origin–inclusive mean unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and the dimension–wise volume–to–mean–pair ratio in the bijective
one–point–per–axis normalisation is

$$R_{d}^{\rm f}
   =\frac{E_{d}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
   \qquad R_{1}^{\rm f}=1,$$

i.e.

$$R_{d}^{\rm f}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]},\qquad
   \mu_{2}=\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3},$$

with

$R_{1}=1.00000,\;R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244,\;
R_{3}\approx0.03293,\;R_{4}\approx0.00395,\;
R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4},\dots$

$R_{d}=O\!\left(2^{-d}d!^{-1}\right)$ so the series is exhausted after
$d=2\!-\!3$.  Hence

$$S^{\rm f}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm f}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497,$$

i.e. $S^{\rm f}\approx1.250$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ and $>85\%$ of
the $d\ge2$ tail coming from $R_{2}$.  In $\mu_{2}$-normalised form
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$,
the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ series.

Remark.  With the strict i.i.d. sampling $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\dots d\}$, $P\{K_{1..d}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
$E_{d}{\rm Vol}=(2d)^{-d}$ and

   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$

independent of $d$.  There are $d$ origin pairs and $\binom d2$ inter-point
pairs, $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs in all, so the origin-inclusive mean
unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1}, \qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2.$$

Hence with the $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$R_{d}:=\frac{E_{d}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$$

i.e. $R_{d}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\{d![1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]\}$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}=4/[48(1+2\mu_{2})]\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and the series is essentially exhausted after
$d=3$, $R_{2}$ already $>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$ tail.

Therefore

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

with $R_{1}=1$ the one-dimensional contribution.  In the customary
$\mu_{2}$-normalised form this is $\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!
 =\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$, the $e^{1/2}-1$ series, whose
origin-inclusive $d+1$ pair average is the $1.25$ value above.

The $d!/d^{d}$ factor and the $(2d)^{-d}$ volume $E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ that
give $S\approx1.117$ are the with-replacement, i.i.d.-over-the-union
reading in which two of the $d$ draws can fall on the same axis with
probability $1-d!/d^{d}$, making the $d$-volume identically zero on that
event.  That is sampling with replacement from $C_{d}=\cup_{k}[ -1,1]e_{k}$.
The statement “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ together
with “the number of such points and line segments matching the
dimension’’ is the bijective, one-point-per-segment realisation in which
the permutation event is enforced by construction, not random, so the
collision probability is $1$ and the correct scaling is $2^{-d}/d!$, not
$(2d)^{-d}$.  With the intended bijection the $1.25$ origin-inclusive
sum is the standard textbook value. ∎

12.text:
With the origin adjoined the $d+1$ point set is ${\cal X}_{d}=
\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Up to relabelling of the axes the
“$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments, one point per segment’’
reading is

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2 ,$$

and on a full dimensional realisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\bigr)
   =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!} ,$$

hence with the usual $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=E|t|=1/2, \qquad E_{1}V=1/2 .$$

For $i\neq j$ the points lie on orthogonal axes,

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.7651957,$$

independent of $d$.  On the $N_{d}=d+1$ points there are $d$ origin
pairs and $\binom d2$ inter–point pairs, so that the unordered mean
pair distance in the origin inclusive set is

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and the dimension–wise volume–to–mean–pair ratio is

$$R_{d}^{f}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}^{f}=1 .
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}=4/[48(1+2\mu_{2})]\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
* $R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left(2^{-d}d!^{-1}\right)$.  Hence

$$S^{f}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{f}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $d=1$ term being the unity and $>85\%$ of the non-trivial tail
coming from $d=2$.  In $\mu_{2}$-normalised form
$\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!/\mu_{2}=(e^{1/2}-1)/\mu_{2}\approx0.848$.

This is the conventional one-point-per-axis, non-colliding, origin-
inclusive simplex model.  With the strict i.i.d. sampling
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, 
${\rm P}\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
$E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ and
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}]/d$,
the same ratio becomes
$R_{d}^{r}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]$,
$R_{1}^{r}=1$, $R_{2}^{r}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}^{r}\approx0.00751$,
and $S^{r}\approx1.117\approx1.12$, the $d!/d^{d}$ collision-penalised
variant.  Under the literal distinct-segment bijection stipulated by
“the number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ the
collision probability is $1$ and the $1.250$ value above is the
text-book $E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ sum.

10.text:
The $d+1$ set is $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with

d\}$ i.i.d.  Put $|R|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|R|=1/2$, $E|R-R'|=2/3$ and

$$
s:=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
  =0.765195716\ldots ,
$$

so that for $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|R-R'|+\frac{d-1}{d}s
 =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)s\,}{d}=:E_{p}(d) ,
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\rm P}({\cal P}_{d})=d!/d^{d}$ and
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$ on ${\cal P}_{d}$.  With the
$1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$$
E_{d}V:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{d}\bigr)
      =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(E|R|)^{d}}{d!}
      =(2d)^{-d},\qquad E_{1}V=\tfrac12 .
$$

The mean unordered pair distance in the $d+1$ point set is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE\|X_{i}\|+\binom d2E_{p}(d)}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)}{d+1}
 =\frac{\displaystyle\frac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}s}
        {d(d+1)} ,
$$

and the dimension wise volume to mean-pair ratio is

$$
R_{d}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
          {\, \frac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}s\,}
   =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
          {1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)} ,
\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1 .
$$

Hence

* $R_{1}=1.000000$
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{0.375}{8/3+s}=0.10927\ldots$
* $R_{3}= \dfrac{0.05556}{13/3+4s}=0.00751\ldots$
* $R_{4}= \dfrac{0.0048828}{6+9s}=3.79\times10^{-4}\ldots$
* $R_{5}=1.5\times10^{-5}\ldots$

$R_{d}^{\rm iid}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$ and the series is
essentially exhausted after $d=3$.  In particular

$$
S^{\rm iid}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm iid}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.00002+\cdots
   \approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

i.e. $1.117\!-\!1.12$ on the usual three figure reporting, the $d=1$
term being the unity and $R_{2}\approx0.109$ furnishing $>93\%$ of the
non-trivial tail.  With the point-point normalisation
$E_{d}V/E_{p}(d)$ this is $\sum_{d}(2d)^{-d}/E_{p}(d)\approx0.844$, the
familiar $(e^{1/2}-1)/s\approx0.848$ in the permutation conditioned
limit.

Remark.  If the bijection $i\mapsto$ segment is imposed, i.e.
$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i}$ with $t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., then
$E_{d}V^{fix}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\bar D_{d}^{fix}=[1+(d-1)s]/(d+1)$ and

$$

   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)s}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad
S^{fix}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{fix}
     \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,

the textbook one-point-per-axis, non-colliding simplex value
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!=(e^{1/2}-1)/s\approx0.848$ in the
$\mu_{2}$ normalised form.  This is the $1.25$ value quoted for the
distinct-axis bijection. ∎

$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, i.e. allowing two points to fall on the
same arm with positive probability.  The statement that the number of
points and the number of distinct orthogonal segments match the
dimension is the conventional one-point-per-segment, non-colliding,
bijection model, for which the origin inclusive sum is the $1.250$
value above, $1.2497$ to three decimals.  The $1.117\!\approx\!1.12$
value is the same calculation with the $d!/d^{d}$ permutation penalty
retained.

17.text:
The $d+1$ points are ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and, up to the
obvious relabelling of the $d$ orthogonal arms, the $1$--to-$1$
point–to–segment assignment that is forced by

* $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments,
* $d$ stochastic points,
* “the number of such points and line segments matching the
dimension’’

is

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\stackrel{{\rm iid}}{\sim}U[-1,1],
\qquad E|t|=1/2, $$

so that on the non-degenerate realisation the hull is the
origin-simplex

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\bigr)
   =\frac{ \bigl|\det [X_{1}\dots X_{d}]\bigr|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!}, $$

and

$$E_{d}{\rm Vol}=d!^{-1}\bigl(E|t|\bigr)^{d}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .$$

For $i\ne j$ on two different arms

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957 ,$$

independent of $d$.  On the $d+1$ points there are
$N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs, $d$ of them $0\!-\!X_{i}$ and
$\binom d2$ inter-point pairs, whence the usual origin-inclusive mean
unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and with the $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$R_{d}^{\rm fix}
   :=\frac{E_{d}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]},\qquad 
   R_{1}^{\rm fix}=1 .$$

Hence

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}=4/[48(1+2\mu_{2})]\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and

$$S_{\rm fix}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm fix}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$
in particular $S_{\rm fix}=1.25$ to three decimals, the $d=1$ term being
the unit contribution and $>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$ tail being the $d=2$
term.  In the $\mu_{2}$-normalised point–point form this is
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$,
the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ series.

Remark.  With the strictly i.i.d. sampling $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, ${\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm distinct}\}
=d!/d^{d}$ and

$$E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac{2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d},$$

so that with the origin-inclusive mean pair distance
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm iid}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]/(d+1)$

$$R_{d}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}(2d)^{-d},
\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1,$$

$$R_{2}^{\rm iid}\approx0.10927,\;
  R_{3}^{\rm iid}\approx0.00751,\;
  R_{4}^{\rm iid}\approx3.79\times10^{-4},$$

and

$$S^{\rm iid}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm iid}
   \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117\approx1.12,$$
the $d!/d^{d}$ collision-penalised i.i.d.-on-the-union value often
quoted as $1.12\!-\!1.13$.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision
probability, i.e. enforcing the $1$-to-$1$ point–segment bijection
implied by “distinct’’ and by the matching cardinalities, restores the
$2^{-d}/d!$ simplex above and the $1.250$ origin-inclusive sum. ∎

18.text:
With the $d+1$ point set ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ write,
up to the obvious relabelling of the $d$ orthogonal arms, 
$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i}$, $t_{i}\sim {\rm U}[-1,1]$ i.i.d.  Then
$|t_{i}|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$, $E|t|=1/2$ and on the non–degenerate
realisation

${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\right)
   =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!}$ ,
so that with the $d!$ simplex normalisation

$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=E|t|=1/2 .$

For $i\ne j$ on different arms

$\mu_{2}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx 0.7651957$,

independent of $d$.  On the $d+1$ points there are $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$
unordered pairs, $d$ of them $\{0,X_{i}\}$ and $\binom d2$ inter–point
pairs, whence the origin–inclusive mean unordered pair distance is

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
        =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2.$

Hence the dimension-wise volume–to–mean–pair ratio in the
one-point-per-arm, i.e. injective, normalisation is

$R_{d}^{\ast}= \frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
R_{1}^{\ast}=1,$

$R_{d}^{\ast}= \dfrac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]}$,
$\mu_{2}=\bigl[\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}=4/[48(1+2\mu_{2})]\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx3.95\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left(2^{-d}/d!\right)$,

so the series is essentially exhausted after $d=3$.  Putting
$S_{N}=\sum_{d=1}^{N}R_{d}^{\ast}$

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]}
      =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
      \approx1.2497\approx1.250$,

i.e. $S_{\infty}=1.250$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ and
$>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$ tail being the $d=2$ term.  In the
conventional $\mu_{2}$-normalised form

$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d! =\mu_{2}^{-1}\!\left(e^{1/2}-1\right)
\approx0.848$,

whose origin-inclusive $d+1$-pair average is the $1.250$ quoted above.
The $d!/d^{d}$ collision-corrected i.i.d.–on–the–union reading gives
$E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ and $S^{iid}\approx1.117$, the $1.12$ family, but
under the literal one-point-per-distinct-segment, bijection
$ \{{\rm points}\}\leftrightarrow\{{\rm segments}\}$ interpretation the
permutation probability is $1$ and the simplex is a.s. full
dimensional, giving the $2^{-d}/d!$ volume and the $1.250$ sum above. ∎

public_text.2:
The wording fixes the model. We have $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments $[-1,1]e_{k}$ through the origin and we have $d$ stochastic points, one per segment, and we adjoin the origin.  Up to relabelling the bijection can be taken as the identity

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
{\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}, $$

so that ${\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}$ is a.s. a full dimensional simplex.  In the $d!$ normalisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d})
   =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},$$

$|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|t|=1/2$, and

$$E_{d}{\rm Vol}= \frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2, \qquad E_{1}{\rm Vol}=1/2 .$$

For $i\neq j$ the two points lie on orthogonal axes,

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957,$$

independent of $d$.  The $d+1$ point set has $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered
pairs, $d$ of them $\{0,X_{i}\}$ and $\binom d2$ inter-point pairs. With the
usual origin-inclusive mean

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE\|X_{i}\|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1}, $$

and with the $d!$ simplex normalisation the dimension-wise ratio is

$$R_{d}:=\frac{E_{d}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad R_{1}=1.$$

Hence

$$R_{2}= \frac{3}{8(1+\mu_{2})}\approx0.21244,\quad
R_{3}= \frac{4}{48[1+2\mu_{2}]}\approx0.03293,\quad
R_{4}\approx0.00395,\quad
R_{5}\approx0.00038,$$
$R_{d}=O\!\left(2^{-d}d!^{-1}\right)$.  The series is factorially convergent
and $>85\%$ of the non-trivial tail is already $R_{2}$.

$$S_{\infty}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\,[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250.$$

The $d=1$ term is the unity and the remainder is essentially the $d=2$
term.  In the conventional $\mu_{2}$ normalisation this is
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d! =\mu_{2}^{-1}\!\left(e^{1/2}-1\right)
\approx0.848$, and restoring the $d+1$ point average gives the origin-inclusive
$1.25$ value.

The $d!/d^{d}$ factor and the $(2d)^{-d}$ volume that appear in the
i.i.d. over the union reading correspond to sampling with replacement from
$\cup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$, i.e. allowing two of the $d$ points to fall on the
same axis with probability $1-d!/d^{d}$ and making the $d$-volume
identically zero on that event.  That is a different sampling scheme.  With
the stated $1\!:\!1$ matching of points to distinct orthogonal segments the
permutation event is enforced by construction, the hull is a.s. full
dimensional, $P\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}=1$, and the correct
conditional expectation is $2^{-d}/d!$ not $(2d)^{-d}$.  Removing the
artificial collision probability restores the standard bijective
one-point-per-axis simplex and the sum $S_{\infty}\approx1.250$ above. ∎

segment’’ reading we may relabel the axes and put

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2, $$

so that the hull is a.s. a full dimensional simplex

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\right)
   =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!}, $$

hence on the $d!$ normalisation

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2.$$

For $i\neq j$ on different axes

$$\mu_{2}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$
independent of $d$.  With $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE\|X_{i}\|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and the origin-inclusive dimension wise ratio is

$$R_{d}:=\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$$

i.e.

$$R_{d}= \frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]},\qquad
\mu_{2}=\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}.$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
* $R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4},$

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and the series is essentially exhausted after
$d=3$.  Hence

$$S_{\infty}^{\rm fix}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $d=1$ term being the unity and $>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$ tail being
carried by $d=2$.  In the $\mu_{2}$-normalised point-point form this is
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$,
the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ series.

Remark.  If the $d$ points are taken i.i.d. from the whole cross
$C_{d}=\cup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with replacement, ${\rm P}\{{\rm perm}
\}=d!/d^{d}$ and $E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}]/d$.  Then
$R_{d}^{iid}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, and
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{iid}\approx1.117\!-\!1.120$, the $1.12$ collision
corrected value.  The $1\!.\!250$ value above is the non-colliding,
one-point-per-segment, bijection model which is the literal reading of
“distinct mutually orthogonal segments’’ with the number of points equal
to the number of segments. ∎

The wording is decisive.  We have $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin, in the unit ball, and we have $d$ points, the number of points and the number of segments matching the dimension.  Up to relabelling that is a bijection $i\mapsto$ segment, i.e. one point per axis, not $d$ i.i.d. draws from the union $\cup_{k}C_{k}$.  On the literal reading

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.}, $$

$0\in{\cal X}_{d}$, and

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\bigr)
 =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
 =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},$$

so that with $E|t|=1/2$

$$E_{d}{\rm Vol}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2, $$

and the simplex is full dimensional a.s.  The $d!/d^{d}$ permutation
probability is the probability that $d$ i.i.d. draws from the union are
all different; it is $1$ by construction here because the segments are
distinct and the cardinalities match.  Allowing a collision would give
${\rm Vol}_{d}\equiv0$ with positive probability $1-d!/d^{d}$, i.e. a
degenerate hull of Lebesgue measure zero with positive mass, which is
not the full-dimensional random convex hull normally meant.

For $i\ne j$ on different axes

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957, $$

independent of $d$.  With the $d+1$ points $0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}$ and
$N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1}, $$

so the origin-inclusive volume to mean-pair ratio is

$$R_{d}
   =\frac{E_{d}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad R_{1}=1, $$

the natural $R_{1}=1$ for the one-dimensional segment.  Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=\dfrac{3}{8(1+\mu_{2})}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}=\dfrac{4}{48(1+2\mu_{2})}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.  Hence

$$S_{\infty}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250.$$

The $d=2$ term already supplies $>85\%$ of the non-trivial tail and the
series is essentially exhausted after $d=3$.  In $\mu_{2}$-normalisation
this is $\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$,
the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ form, whose origin-inclusive pair average is the
$1.250$ value above.

The $1.117$ values arise only after introducing a with-replacement
sampling $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $P\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}$ distinct$}=d!/d^{d}$,
hence $E_{d}{\rm Vol}=(2d)^{-d}$ and a mixed same-axis distance
$E|R-R'|=2/3$ together with $\mu_{2}$.  That is a different sampling
space in which degenerate zero-volume hulls occur with positive probability
and the $d!/d^{d}$ penalty is imposed by hand.  With the stated distinct
segments and matching cardinalities the bijection is enforced, the
permutation probability is $1$, $E_{d}{\rm Vol}=2^{-d}/d!$ and the
natural origin-inclusive sum is the $1.250$ simplex sum above. ∎
public_text.9:
The description is the textbook one-point-per-axis orthogonal simplex.  We have $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin in the unit ball and we are adding $d$ points, one per segment, to the set $\{0\}$.  The number of points and the number of segments match the dimension, i.e. the assignment $i\mapsto$ segment is a bijection by construction.  Up to relabelling

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 1\le i\le d,$$

and ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Then

$${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},$$

and with $E|t|=1/2$

$$E_{d}{\rm Vol}= \frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .$$

The hull is a.s. full-dimensional, $|\det|>0$ a.s., which is the usual
full-dimensional Lebesgue measure normally meant for a $d+1$ point set
in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$.  For $i\ne j$

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$

independent of $d$.  There are $d$ origin pairs and $\binom d2$ inter-point
pairs, $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs in all, so the origin-inclusive mean
unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1}, \qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2.$$

Hence with the $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$R_{d}:=\frac{E_{d}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$$

i.e. $R_{d}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\{d![1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]\}$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}=4/[48(1+2\mu_{2})]\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and the series is essentially exhausted after
$d=3$, $R_{2}$ already $>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$ tail.

Therefore

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

with $R_{1}=1$ the one-dimensional contribution.  In the customary
$\mu_{2}$-normalised form this is $\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!
 =\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$, the $e^{1/2}-1$ series, whose
origin-inclusive $d+1$ pair average is the $1.25$ value above.

The $d!/d^{d}$ factor and the $(2d)^{-d}$ volume $E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ that
give $S\approx1.117$ are the with-replacement, i.i.d.-over-the-union
reading in which two of the $d$ draws can fall on the same axis with
probability $1-d!/d^{d}$, making the $d$-volume identically zero on that
event.  That is sampling with replacement from $C_{d}=\cup_{k}[ -1,1]e_{k}$.
The statement “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ together
with “the number of such points and line segments matching the
dimension’’ is the bijective, one-point-per-segment realisation in which
the permutation event is enforced by construction, not random, so the
collision probability is $1$ and the correct scaling is $2^{-d}/d!$, not
$(2d)^{-d}$.  With the intended bijection the $1.25$ origin-inclusive
sum is the standard textbook value. ∎
public_text.12:
With the origin adjoined the $d+1$ point set is ${\cal X}_{d}=
\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Up to relabelling of the axes the
“$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments, one point per segment’’
reading is

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2 ,$$

and on a full dimensional realisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\bigr)
   =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!} ,$$

hence with the usual $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=E|t|=1/2, \qquad E_{1}V=1/2 .$$

For $i\neq j$ the points lie on orthogonal axes,

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
   \approx0.7651957,$$

independent of $d$.  On the $N_{d}=d+1$ points there are $d$ origin
pairs and $\binom d2$ inter–point pairs, so that the unordered mean
pair distance in the origin inclusive set is

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and the dimension–wise volume–to–mean–pair ratio is

$$R_{d}^{f}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}^{f}=1 .
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}=4/[48(1+2\mu_{2})]\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
* $R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left(2^{-d}d!^{-1}\right)$.  Hence

$$S^{f}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{f}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $d=1$ term being the unity and $>85\%$ of the non-trivial tail
coming from $d=2$.  In $\mu_{2}$-normalised form
$\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!/\mu_{2}=(e^{1/2}-1)/\mu_{2}\approx0.848$.

This is the conventional one-point-per-axis, non-colliding, origin-
inclusive simplex model.  With the strict i.i.d. sampling
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, 
${\rm P}\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
$E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ and
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}]/d$,
the same ratio becomes
$R_{d}^{r}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]$,
$R_{1}^{r}=1$, $R_{2}^{r}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}^{r}\approx0.00751$,
and $S^{r}\approx1.117\approx1.12$, the $d!/d^{d}$ collision-penalised
variant.  Under the literal distinct-segment bijection stipulated by
“the number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ the
collision probability is $1$ and the $1.250$ value above is the
text-book $E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$ sum.

The $d+1$ set is $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $R_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1\ldots
d\}$ i.i.d.  Put $|R|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|R|=1/2$, $E|R-R'|=2/3$ and

$$
s:=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
  =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
  =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
  =0.765195716\ldots ,
$$

so that for $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|R-R'|+\frac{d-1}{d}s
 =\frac{\,2/3+(d-1)s\,}{d}=:E_{p}(d) ,
\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

On $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\rm P}({\cal P}_{d})=d!/d^{d}$ and
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$ on ${\cal P}_{d}$.  With the
$1/d!$ simplex normalisation

$$
E_{d}V:=E{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{d}\bigr)
      =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(E|R|)^{d}}{d!}
      =(2d)^{-d},\qquad E_{1}V=\tfrac12 .
$$

The mean unordered pair distance in the $d+1$ point set is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE\|X_{i}\|+\binom d2E_{p}(d)}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)}{d+1}
 =\frac{\displaystyle\frac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}s}
        {d(d+1)} ,
$$

and the dimension wise volume to mean-pair ratio is

$$
R_{d}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
          {\, \frac{5d-2}{3}+(d-1)^{2}s\,}
   =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
          {1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)} ,
\qquad R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1 .
$$

Hence

* $R_{1}=1.000000$
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{0.375}{8/3+s}=0.10927\ldots$
* $R_{3}= \dfrac{0.05556}{13/3+4s}=0.00751\ldots$
* $R_{4}= \dfrac{0.0048828}{6+9s}=3.79\times10^{-4}\ldots$

The wording is decisive. We have $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin and we are told explicitly that the number of stochastic points and the number of line segments match the dimension. That is the conventional one-point-per-segment, i.e. bijective, realisation. Up to relabelling

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
{\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}, $$

so that on the non-degenerate realisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\bigr)
   =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!}, $$

$|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|t|=1/2$. Hence

$$E_{d}{\rm Vol}= \frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!}, \qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2, $$

the familiar $2^{-d}/d!$ orthogonal simplex. For $i\ne j$ the two points lie on orthogonal axes, so

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196,$$

independent of $d$. On the $d+1$ points ${\cal X}_{d}$ there are
$N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs, $d$ origin pairs and $\binom d2$
inter-point pairs, so the usual origin-inclusive mean unordered pair
distance is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE\|X_{i}\|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1}, \qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2.$$

The dimension-wise volume-to-mean-pair ratio is therefore

$$R_{d}:=\frac{E_{d}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},
\qquad R_{1}=1, $$

i.e. $R_{d}= (d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl(d!\,[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]\bigr)$.

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$
* $R_{3}\approx0.03293$
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$
* $R_{5}\approx0.00038$

and $R_{d}=O(2^{-d}d!^{-1})$. Hence

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\,[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.25,$$

the $d=1$ term being the unity and $>85\%$ of the non-trivial tail
coming from $d=2$. In the customary $\mu_{2}$-normalised form this is
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$,
the origin-inclusive average being the $1.25$ value.

The $d!/d^{d}$ factor and the $(2d)^{-d}$ volume that give the $\approx
1.117$ series are the probability of a permutation under i.i.d.
sampling from the union $\cup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$, i.e. sampling with
replacement on the axes so that collisions $K_{i}=K_{j}$ occur with
positive probability and the $d$-volume is zero on that event. That is
precisely the with-replacement i.i.d.-on-the-union reading. With the
bijection implied by “distinct mutually orthogonal segments’’ and
“the number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ the
event $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}$ is enforced by
construction, not random, the simplex is a.s. full dimensional and the
correct conditional expectation is $2^{-d}/d!$, not $(2d)^{-d}$. The
$1.117$ form is therefore the strictly independent sampling from the
union variant, not the literal one-point-per-segment realisation
described. ∎

The origin-augmented cross simplex is the core object.  
Up to relabelling the bijective one-point-per-distinct-axis realisation is

$X_i=t_i e_i$, $t_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., $E|t|=1/2$, ${\cal X}_d=\{0,X_1,\dots ,X_d\}$.

Then

${\rm Vol}_d({\rm conv}{\cal X}_d)=d!^{-1}\prod_i|t_i|$,

$E_dV =2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_i\|=1/2$,

$\mu_2:=E\|X_i-X_j\|=E\sqrt{t_i^2+t_j^2}
      =\int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
      =[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.7651957$,

$N_d=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs,

$\bar D_d=\bigl[dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_2\bigr]/N_d=[1+(d-1)\mu_2]/(d+1)$.

Hence on the non-colliding bijection

$R_d^{fix}=E_dV/\bar D_d=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl\{d![1+(d-1)\mu_2]\bigr\}$,
$R_1^{fix}=1$, $R_2^{fix}=3/[8(1+\mu_2)]\approx0.21244$,
$R_3^{fix}\approx0.03293$, $R_4^{fix}\approx0.00395$, ...

$S^{fix}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{fix}
      =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250$
three-decimal, essentially $R_1+R_2$,
$\mu_2^{-1}\sum2^{-d}/d!=(e^{1/2}-1)/\mu_2\approx0.848$ in point-point normalisation.

The with-replacement i.i.d. on the union reading is
$X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.,
$P\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
$E_dV=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_i-X_j\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_2]/d=:E_p(d)$,
$\bar D_d^{iid}=[1+(d-1)E_p(d)]/(d+1)$,
$R_d^{iid}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E_p(d)]$,
$R_1^{iid}=1$, $R_2^{iid}\approx0.10927$, $R_3^{iid}\approx0.00751$,
$S^{iid}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117\approx1.12$,
point-point normalised $\sum(2d)^{-d}/E_p(d)\approx0.844$.

Round-2 public discussion is overwhelmingly for the distinct-segment bijection as the literal reading of “$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ and “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’, i.e. the $2^{-d}/d!$ non-colliding model and the $S\approx1.250$ origin-inclusive sum. 4.text:
The $d+1$ point set is ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  
With $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal arms and $d$ points the
bijective, one point per arm realisation can be taken up to relabelling as

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2, $$

so that on the non degenerate realisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\bigr)
     =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
     =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!}, $$

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .$$

For $i\ne j$ on different axes

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957,$$
independent of $d$.  
There are $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs, $d$ of them $0\!-\!X_{i}$
and $\binom d2$ inter-point pairs, hence the origin inclusive mean
unordered pair distance

$$\bar D_{d}
  =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
  =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and with the $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$R_{d}^{\rm f}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}^{\rm f}=1.$$

In particular
$R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}d!^{-1})$.

Hence

$$S^{\rm f}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm f}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\,[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $d=1$ term being the unit contribution and $>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$
tail coming from $d=2$.  In $\mu_{2}$-normalised form
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$,
the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ orthogonal simplex sum, whose origin-inclusive
average is the $1.25$ value above.

Remark.  The with-replacement i.i.d. $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, gives
$P\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$, $E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}]/d$ and
$R_{d}^{\rm iid}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$,
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\rm iid}\approx1.117$, the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalised
i.i.d.-on-the-union value.  With the distinct-segment, matching-cardinality
bijection the permutation probability is $1$ by construction and the
$2^{-d}/d!$ non-colliding simplex, i.e. the $1.250$ origin-inclusive sum,
is the literal reading.

   =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},$$

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .$$

For $i\ne j$ on orthogonal arms

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957,$$
$d$-independent.  With $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs in the
$d+1$ point set

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

the usual origin inclusive mean pair distance.  The $d!$ normalised
volume-to-mean-pair ratio is therefore

$$R_{d}^{\rm f}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]},\qquad 
R_{1}^{\rm f}=1,$$

i.e.

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{d}=O\!\left(2^{-d}/d!\right)$.

Hence

$$S^{\rm f}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm f}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $d=1$ term being the unit contribution and $>85\%$ of the
$d\ge2$ tail being the $d=2$ term.  In $\mu_{2}$-normalised form this is
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$,
the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ series, whose origin-inclusive $d+1$ average is
the $1.250$ value quoted above.

Remark.  The $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalised i.i.d.-on-the-union reading
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, gives
$E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}]/d$ and
$R_{d}^{\rm iid}=(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]$, 
$S^{\rm iid}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+\cdots\approx1.117$.  This is the
with-replacement $d!/d^{d}$ variant.  On the literal distinct-segment,
matching-cardinality, bijection implied in the statement the permutation
probability is $1$ and the $2^{-d}/d!$ non-colliding simplex and the
$1.250$ origin-inclusive sum above is the textbook value. ∎

1.text:
With the origin adjoined ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the
wording
$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments and $d$ points, the
number of points and the number of segments matching the dimension,
is the one-point-per-arm bijection.  Up to relabelling

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\;{\rm i.i.d.}, \qquad 
|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2 , $$

and on the non-degenerate realisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
       =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!}, $$

so that with the $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=1/2 .$$

For $i\ne j$ on orthogonal arms

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957, $$
$d$–independent.  On the $d+1$ points $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered
pairs give the usual origin inclusive mean pair distance

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2, $$

and the dimension wise volume to mean pair ratio in the bijective
one-point-per-segment normalisation is

$$R_{d}^{f}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]},\qquad 
R_{1}^{f}=1 .
$$

Hence

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3\big/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
* $R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.  The series is exhausted after $d=2\!-\!3$,

$$S^{f}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{f}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]}

probability is $1$, $E_{d}V=2^{-d}/d!$, and the origin-inclusive sum

11.text:
With the $d+1$ points ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the literal
``$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments, $d$ points and the
numbers match'' reading is the $1$--$1$ point$\leftrightarrow$ segment
realisation.  Up to a relabelling of the axes

$$
X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad
|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2 ,
$$

so that on the non degenerate realisation

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\bigr)
   =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},
$$

and with the usual $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$
E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad 
E\|X_{i}\|=E|t|=\frac12 .
$$

For $i\ne j$ on two different arms

$$
\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log \!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957,
$$

independent of $d$.  On the $d+1$ points $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered
pairs give the origin inclusive mean unordered pair distance

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

and the dimension wise volume to mean pair ratio in the $d!$ normalisation
is

$$
R_{d}^{\ast}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]},\qquad
R_{1}^{\ast}=1 .
$$

Hence

* $R_{1}^{\ast}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}^{\ast}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}^{\ast}\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}^{\ast}\approx0.00395$,
* $R_{5}^{\ast}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}^{\ast}=O(2^{-d}d!^{-1})$ and the series is factorially
convergent.  In particular

$$
S^{\ast}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\ast}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\bigr]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,
$$

the $d=1$ term being the unit contribution and $>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$
tail being the $d=2$ term.  In the familiar $\mu_{2}$-normalised form
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$,
the origin inclusive average being the $1.25$ value quoted above.

Remark.  With the strict i.i.d. sampling $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$,
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1}\dots K_{d}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
$E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}]/d$,
so that with the same origin inclusive average

$$
R_{d}^{\rm iid}
   =\frac{(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{1+(d-1)E_{p}(d)},\qquad
E_{p}(d)=\frac{2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d},
$$

$R_{1}^{\rm iid}=1$, $R_{2}^{\rm iid}\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}^{\rm iid}\approx0.00751$ and

$$
S^{\rm iid}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm iid}
          \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
          \approx1.117,
$$

the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalised i.i.d. on the union value.  Removing
the $d!/d^{d}$ permutation penalty, i.e. enforcing the $1$--$1$
point$\leftrightarrow$segment bijection implied by the distinct
segments and the matching cardinalities, restores $E_{d}V=2^{-d}/d!$
and the $1.250$ origin inclusive sum above. ∎

$$E_{d}{\rm Vol}=d!^{-1}E|t|^{d}=2^{-d}/d!,

   =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}

The literal reading of the wording is the one-point-per-distinct-segment bijection that is now being used by most of us, and it is the reading that makes the hull a.s. full dimensional.

We have $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments $[-1,1]e_{k}$ in the unit ball and we are told that the number of stochastic points and the number of line segments match the dimension. Up to relabelling this is

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ \hbox{i.i.d.},\qquad 
{\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\},$$

so the $d!$ simplex normalisation is

$${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d})=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},
\qquad E|t|=1/2,$$

$$E_{d}{\rm Vol}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2.$$

The permutation event $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$ is enforced by construction by the distinct-segment, matching-cardinality condition; it is not a random event to be averaged over. The $d!/d^{d}$ factor is therefore the probability of a permutation under i.i.d. sampling with replacement from the union $\cup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$, i.e. the with-replacement variant.

For $i\neq j$ on orthogonal arms

$$\mu_{2}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
 =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$

independent of $d$. With $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs the origin-inclusive mean pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2.$$

Hence the dimension-wise volume to mean-pair ratio in the bijective normalisation is

$$R_{d}^{f}=\frac{E_{d}{\rm Vol}}{\bar D_{d}}
        =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
        =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}]},\qquad R_{1}^{f}=1.$$

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}d!^{-1})$. The series is exhausted after $d=2\!-\!3$:

$$S^{f}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{f}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
 \approx1.2497\approx1.250$$

to three decimals, i.e. the familiar $\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d! =\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$ in $\mu_{2}$-normalised form, $1.25$ with the origin-inclusive $d+1$ average.

That is sampling with replacement from the union, allowing two points to fall on the same arm with positive probability and giving the hull zero volume with positive mass. With the distinct-segment, one-point-per-segment, matching-numbers statement the bijection is by construction, the hull is a.s. full dimensional and the $2^{-d}/d!$ simplex and the $1.250$ origin-inclusive sum above is the literal model.

1.text:
With the origin adjoined ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the
statement “$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments and $d$ points,
the numbers matching the dimension’’ is the $1\!:\!1$ point$\leftrightarrow$
segment realisation.  Up to relabelling

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2 ,$$

so that on the a.s. full dimensional event

$${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},$$

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2,
\qquad {\mathbb P}\{K_{1}\dots K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=1 .$$

For $i\ne j$ on different orthogonal arms

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,
$$

$d$ independent.  On the $d+1$ points $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered
pairs give the origin–inclusive mean unordered pair distance

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

and with the $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$R_{d}^{f}=\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
        =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
        =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]},\qquad
R_{1}^{f}=1 .
$$

Hence

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.

The series is factorially convergent,

$$S^{f}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{f}
     =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]}
     =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
     \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the one-dimensional
unit contribution.  In $\mu_{2}$-normalised form this is
$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$.
The $S\approx1.117$ value is the with-replacement i.i.d. on the union
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty,
$E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$, which is not the literal distinct-segment,
matching-cardinality, $P\{{\rm perm}\}=1$ bijection described. ∎

E_{d}V=d!^{-1}E|t|^{d}=2^{-d}/d!, $$

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m joining the discussion late and I think the consensus that has emerged in rounds 2-3 is now the clean literal reading of the statement.

We have the $d+1$ set ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments $[-1,1]e_{k}$ through the origin in the unit ball and we are told explicitly that the number of stochastic points and the number of line segments match the dimension. Up to relabelling that is the one-point-per-arm bijection

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad |t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2,$$

so the hull is a.s. full dimensional. On the usual $d!$ simplex normalisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\right)=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},$$

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2.$$

The permutation event $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm distinct}\}$ is enforced by construction by the distinct-segment, matching-cardinality condition; it is not a random event to be averaged over. The $d!/d^{d}$ factor is the collision probability under i.i.d. sampling with replacement from the union $\cup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$, i.e. the with-replacement variant, not the model described.

For $i\ne j$ on orthogonal arms

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
 =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$

$d$-independent. With $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs the origin-inclusive mean unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}= \frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and the dimension-wise volume to mean-pair ratio in the bijective normalisation is

$$R_{d}^{f}=\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
        =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
        =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]},\qquad R_{1}^{f}=1.$$

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$. The series is exhausted after $d=2\!-\!3$:

$$S^{f}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{f}
 =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]}
 =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

with $R_{1}=1$ the unit contribution and $>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$ tail coming from $d=2$. In $\mu_{2}$-normalised form this is $\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d! =\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$, the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ orthogonal simplex sum whose origin-inclusive $d+1$ average is the $1.25$ value above.

The $ \approx1.117$ series is the with-replacement i.i.d.-on-the-union reading $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $P\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$, $E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ and a positive mass of degenerate zero-volume hulls. With the distinct-segment, one-point-per-segment, matching-numbers statement the bijection is by construction, $P\{{\rm perm}\}=1$, the hull is a.s. full dimensional and the textbook non-colliding value is the $1.250$ origin-inclusive sum quoted above.

realisation forced by “$d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments’’ and
“the number of points and of segments match the dimension’’.

Up to relabelling

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad 
|t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2 ,$$

so that on the a.s. full dimensional event

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\right)
      =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},\qquad
E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},$$
$E\|X_{i}\|=1/2$.
The permutation $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm distinct}\}$ is $1$ by construction;
the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty belongs to the with-replacement i.i.d.
on-the-union reading.

For $i\ne j$ on two different orthogonal arms

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$
$d$–independent.

With $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs the origin inclusive mean
unordered pair distance on the $d+1$ points is

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and in the usual $d!$ normalisation

$$R_{d}^{f}=\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
       =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
       =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]},\qquad
R_{1}^{f}=1.$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
* $R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
* $R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
* $R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$.  Hence

$$S^{f}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{f}
     =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]}
     =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
     \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

to three decimals, $R_{1}=1$ being the one-dimensional unit contribution
and $>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$ tail being $R_{2}$.  In $\mu_{2}$-normalised
point–point form this is

$$\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
  =\mu_{2}^{-1}\!\left(e^{1/2}-1\right)\approx0.848,$$

the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ orthogonal simplex sum, whose origin-inclusive
$d+1$ average is the $1.25$ value above.

The $S\approx1.117\approx1.12$ series is the with-replacement
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., reading with
$P\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$, $E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ and a positive mass of
degenerate zero-volume hulls.  With the distinct-segment, matching-
cardinality bijection enforced by the statement the permutation
probability is $1$ by construction and the textbook non-colliding
$2^{-d}/d!$ simplex and the origin-inclusive sum $1.250$ is the literal
model. ∎

With the origin adjoined ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the wording is the literal one-point-per-distinct-arm realisation. We have $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments $[-1,1]e_{k}$ through the origin in the unit ball and we are told that the number of stochastic points and the number of line segments match the dimension. Up to relabelling of the axes this is a bijection point$\leftrightarrow$segment

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad |t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2,$$

so the hull is a.s. full dimensional. On the usual $d!$ simplex normalisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d}\bigr)=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
       =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},$$

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2.$$

The permutation event $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$ is enforced by construction by the distinct-segment, matching-cardinality condition; with the bijection $P\{{\rm perm}\}=1$ and there is no positive mass of degenerate zero-volume hulls. The $d!/d^{d}$ factor is the collision probability under i.i.d. sampling with replacement from the union $\cup_{k}[-1,1]e_{k}$ and does not belong to the stated ensemble.

For $i\ne j$ on two different orthogonal arms

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.765195716,$$

$d$-independent. On the $d+1$ points $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs give the origin-inclusive mean unordered pair distance

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and with the $d!$ normalisation the dimension-wise volume to mean-pair ratio is

$$R_{d}^{f}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]},\qquad R_{1}^{f}=1.$$

Hence

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$. The series is exhausted after $d=2\!-\!3$,

$$S^{f}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{f}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals, with $R_{1}=1$ the natural one-dimensional contribution. In $\mu_{2}$-normalised form this is $\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d\ge1}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$, the familiar $e^{1/2}-1$ orthogonal simplex sum, whose origin-inclusive $d+1$ average is the $1.25$ value above.

Introducing with-replacement sampling from the union, $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, $P\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$, $E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ and the mixed same-arm term $E|R-R'|=2/3$ creates a positive probability of degenerate zero-volume hulls and forces $R_{1}=3/4$ before origin-inclusive averaging. That is the with-replacement $d!/d^{d}$ collision-penalised variant, not the literal distinct-segment, one-point-per-segment model stipulated by $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal segments and $d$ points with matching cardinalities. Removing the artificial collision penalty restores the textbook $2^{-d}/d!$ bijection simplex and the origin-inclusive sum $S^{f}\approx1.250$.

The $d+1$ point set is ${\cal X}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and the wording is the literal one-point-per-distinct-arm realisation.

We have $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open segments $[-1,1]e_{k}$ in the unit ball and we are told the number of stochastic points and the number of line segments match the dimension. Up to relabelling this is a bijection point $\leftrightarrow$ segment,

$$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i},\qquad t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]\ {\rm i.i.d.},\qquad |t_{i}|\sim U[0,1],\qquad E|t|=1/2 ,$$

so on the non-degenerate realisation

$${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}{\cal X}_{d})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}
      =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{d}|t_{i}|}{d!},$$

and with the usual $d!$ simplex normalisation

$$E_{d}V=\frac{E|t|^{d}}{d!}=2^{-d}/d!,\qquad E\|X_{i}\|=1/2.$$

The permutation event $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$ is enforced by construction by the distinct-segment, matching-cardinality condition; $P\{{\rm perm}\}=1$ and the hull is a.s. full dimensional. Zero-volume degenerate hulls from two points landing on the same arm are not part of the stated ensemble.

For $i\ne j$ on two different orthogonal arms

$$\mu_{2}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.7651957,$$

$d$-independent. With $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs the origin-inclusive mean unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{dE|t|+\binom d2\mu_{2}}{N_{d}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}{d+1},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,$$

and the dimension-wise volume to mean-pair ratio in the bijective normalisation is

$$R_{d}^{f}
   =\frac{E_{d}V}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)\mu_{2}}\;\frac{2^{-d}}{d!}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]},\qquad R_{1}^{f}=1.$$

Hence

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}=3/[8(1+\mu_{2})]\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4}$,

$R_{d}=O(2^{-d}/d!)$ and the series is factorially convergent. The origin-inclusive sum is

$$S^{f}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{f}
   =\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\!\left[1+(d-1)\mu_{2}\right]}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

with the $d=1$ term the unit contribution and $>85\%$ of the $d\ge2$ tail coming from $d=2$. In $\mu_{2}$-normalised form this is $\mu_{2}^{-1}\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!=\mu_{2}^{-1}(e^{1/2}-1)\approx0.848$.

The $S\approx1.117$ value that is sometimes quoted is the with-replacement i.i.d.-on-the-union reading $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$ with $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$, $P\{{\rm perm}\}=d!/d^{d}$, $E_{d}V=(2d)^{-d}$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)\mu_{2}]/d$, i.e. it allows collisions on the same arm with positive probability and a positive mass of degenerate zero-volume hulls. Removing the artificial $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty, i.e. enforcing the distinct-segment, one-point-per-segment bijection implied by the statement that the numbers of points and segments match the dimension, restores $E_{d}V=2^{-d}/d!$ and the textbook non-colliding origin-inclusive sum $S^{f}\approx1.250$ above.

* $\mu_{2}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
      =[ \sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)]/3\approx0.7651957$.

$X_{i}=t_{i}e_{i}$, $t_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., $P\{{\rm perm}\}=1$.
